translations.literal: Volume 204, Biographies 129: Occult Arts and Techniques (Wikisource header with Northern Song period, links to volumes 203 and 205, and notes listing Li Chunfeng; Zhen Quan (Xu Yinzong, Zhang Wenzong); Yuan Tiangang (Keshi, Zhang Jingzang, Yifu Sil, Jin Liangfeng, Wang Yuanzhi); Xue Yi (Ye Fashan); Ming Chongyan; Shang Xianfu; Yan Shansi; Du Sheng; Zhang Guo (Xing Hebao, Shi Yeguang, Luo Siyuan); Jiang Fu; Sang Daomao).
translations.idiomatic: Wikisource chapter banner for Volume 204, Biographies 129 — Occult Arts and Techniques; navigational links to volumes 203 and 205; notes list Li Chunfeng, Zhen Quan (with Xu Yinzong and Zhang Wenzong), Yuan Tiangang (with Keshi, Zhang Jingzang, Yifu Sil, Jin Liangfeng, and Wang Yuanzhi), Xue Yi (with Ye Fashan), Ming Chongyan, Shang Xianfu, Yan Shansi, Du Sheng, Zhang Guo (with Xing Hebao, Shi Yeguang, and Luo Siyuan), Jiang Fu, and Sang Daomao.

sentences.zh: 凡推步、卜、相、醫、巧，皆技也。

translations.literal: All of calendrical calculation, divination, physiognomy, medicine, and craft are techniques.
translations.idiomatic: Calendrical astronomy, divination, physiognomy, medicine, and mechanical craft—all count as specialized techniques.

sentences.zh: 能以技自顯地一世，亦悟之天，非積習致然。

translations.literal: Those who can make a technique display itself in one generation also have awakened to Heaven; it is not that accumulated practice alone brings this about.
translations.idiomatic: When someone can rise to fame in a single age through a craft alone, that gift is also a kind of heaven-sent insight—not something mere long practice can fully explain.

sentences.zh: 然士君子能之，則不迂，不泥，不矜，不神；

translations.literal: Yet when gentlemen and superior men can do them, they are not pedantic, not stuck, not boastful, and not mystical;
translations.idiomatic: When gentlemen master such arts, they are neither pedantic nor rigid, neither boastful nor given to mystification;

sentences.zh: 小人能之，則迂而入諸拘礙，泥而弗通大方，矜以誇眾，神以誣人，故前聖不以為教，蓋吝之也。

translations.literal: when petty men can do them, they become pedantic and fall into every constraint, stick fast and fail to reach the larger pattern, boast to dazzle the crowd, and mystify to deceive people. Therefore the former sages did not take these as teaching—they were sparing of them.
translations.idiomatic: but when petty men do, they turn pedantic and trap themselves in narrow rules, cling to method and miss the larger view, strut to impress crowds, and play the wonder-worker to mislead others. That is why the ancient sages did not treat such skills as proper instruction—they held them back.

sentences.zh: 若李淳風諫太宗不濫誅，許胤宗不著方劑書，嚴譔諫不合乾陵，乃卓然有益於時者，茲可珍也。

translations.literal: As when Li Chunfeng admonished Taizong not to execute people indiscriminately, Xu Yinzong refused to write books of prescriptions, and Yan Zan admonished against joining the Qianling tomb—such men stood out as truly beneficial to their age; these are to be treasured.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chunfeng's counsel to Emperor Taizong against indiscriminate killing, Xu Yinzong's refusal to publish formula books, and Yan Zan's protest against the Qianling mausoleum project—all stand out as men who genuinely served their times. Such figures are worth cherishing.

sentences.zh: 至遠知、果、撫等詭行紀怪，又技之下者焉。

translations.literal: As for Yuanzhi, Guo, Fu, and the like, with their freakish conduct and records of marvels—they are yet lower among the techniques.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Wang Yuanzhi, Zhang Guo, and Jiang Fu, with their eccentric deeds and tales of the uncanny, belong to an even lower rung of the craft.

sentences.zh: 李淳風，岐州雍人。

translations.literal: Li Chunfeng was a native of Yong in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chunfeng came from Yong in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 父播，仕隋高唐尉，棄官為道士，號黃冠子，以論譔自見。

translations.literal: His father Bo served the Sui as magistrate of Gaotang, abandoned office to become a Daoist priest, styled himself Huangguanzi, and made himself known through treatises and writings.
translations.idiomatic: His father Li Bo had served the Sui as magistrate of Gaotang, then left office to become a Daoist priest under the name Huangguanzi and won notice through scholarly writings.

sentences.zh: 淳風幼爽秀，通群書，明步天歷算。

translations.literal: Chunfeng in youth was bright and elegant, mastered the classics broadly, and was skilled in pacing heaven and calendrical calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Chunfeng was clever and refined as a boy, read widely, and excelled in astronomy and calendrical mathematics.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，與傅仁均爭歷法，議者多附淳風，故以將仁郎直太史局。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he disputed the calendar with Fu Renjun; most of those in the debate sided with Chunfeng, so he was appointed Jiangrenlang on duty at the Astronomical Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan reign he debated the calendar with Fu Renjun; most court opinion favored Chunfeng, and he was posted to the Astronomical Bureau as a Jiangrenlang.

sentences.zh: 制渾得儀，詆摭前世失，著《法象書》七篇上之。

translations.literal: He made a armillary sphere and obtained the instruments, criticized and gathered the errors of previous ages, and presented seven chapters of the Faxiang shu.
translations.idiomatic: He built an armillary sphere and related instruments, catalogued earlier calendrical errors, and submitted seven chapters of his Book of Celestial Patterns.

sentences.zh: 擢承務郎，遷太常博士，改太史丞，與諸儒修書，遷為令。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Chengwulang, moved to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, changed to Vice Director of the Astronomical Bureau, joined the Confucian scholars in compiling books, and was advanced to Director.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Chengwulang, then Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, he became Vice Director of the Astronomical Bureau, took part in the great book project with other scholars, and rose to Director of the bureau.

sentences.zh: 太宗得秘讖，言「唐中弱，有女武代王」。

translations.literal: Taizong obtained a secret prophecy saying, "Tang will weaken at its middle; a woman of martial aspect will replace the king."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong came upon a secret prophecy: "Tang will grow feeble midway; a martial woman will seize the throne."

sentences.zh: 以問淳風，對曰：「其兆既成，已在宮中。

translations.literal: He asked Chunfeng, who replied, "The omen is already fulfilled; she is already in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Chunfeng, who answered, "The omen is already fulfilled—the person is already in the palace.

sentences.zh: 又四十年而王，王而夷唐子孫且盡。」

translations.literal: In another forty years she will be king; once king she will exterminate Tang's descendants to the last."
translations.idiomatic: In another forty years she will reign, and once enthroned she will wipe out Tang's line almost entirely."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我求而殺之，奈何？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "If I search her out and kill her, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If I hunt her down and kill her, what then?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「天之所命，不可去也，而王者果不死，徒使疑似之戳淫及無辜。

translations.literal: He replied, "What Heaven has ordained cannot be removed; yet one destined to be king truly will not die—killing her would only spread suspicion's punishment wantonly upon the innocent.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Heaven's mandate cannot be undone. A future sovereign will not die from your blade; you would only spread suspicion and slaughter among the innocent.

sentences.zh: 且陛下所親愛，四十年而老，老則仁，雖受終易姓，而不能絕唐。

translations.literal: Moreover she is one Your Majesty loves; in forty years she will be old, and in old age she will be humane. Though in the end she receives the throne and changes the surname, she cannot extinguish Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, she is someone you cherish. In forty years she will be old, and age will soften her. Though the throne changes hands at last, Tang itself cannot be utterly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 若殺之，復生壯者，多殺而逞，則陛下子孫無遺種矣！」

translations.literal: If you kill her, another vigorous one will arise; with many killings she will prevail, and then Your Majesty's descendants will leave no seed!"
translations.idiomatic: Kill her, and a younger, stronger claimant will appear. The more you kill, the bolder such omens grow—and Your Majesty's line will leave no survivor!"

sentences.zh: 帝采其言，止。

translations.literal: The emperor took his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his counsel and desisted.

sentences.zh: 淳風於占候吉兇，若節契然，當世術家意有鬼神相之，非學習可致，終不能測也。

translations.literal: Chunfeng in observing and awaiting fortune and misfortune was like tally-marks on bamboo slips; the technicians of the age thought spirits and gods assisted him—what study could bring this?—and in the end none could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: In divining good and ill fortune Chunfeng was uncannily exact, as if reading off tallies. Contemporary experts believed spirits aided him—no mere training could explain it—and no one could finally plumb his methods.

sentences.zh: 以勞封昌樂縣男。

translations.literal: For merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Changle county.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was enfeoffed as Baron of Changle.

sentences.zh: 奉詔與算博士梁述、助教王真儒等是正《五曹》、《孫子》等書，刊定註解，立於學官。

translations.literal: By imperial order he joined Calculation Erudite Liang Shu, Assistant Instructor Wang Zhenru, and others to rectify the Wucao, Sunzi, and other books, revise and fix their commentaries, and establish them in the schools.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he worked with Calculation Erudite Liang Shu, Assistant Instructor Wang Zhenru, and others to collate the Wucao, Sunzi, and related mathematical texts, settle their commentaries, and place them in the official curriculum.

sentences.zh: 撰《麟德歷》代《戊寅歷》，候者推最密。

translations.literal: He compiled the Lindé Calendar to replace the Wuyin Calendar; observers who calculated found it the most precise.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Lindé Calendar to replace the Wuyin Calendar, and astronomers judged its predictions the most accurate yet.

sentences.zh: 自秘閣郎中復為太史令，卒。

translations.literal: From Secretariat Drafter he returned to Director of the Astronomical Bureau and died.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as Secretariat Drafter he again became Director of the Astronomical Bureau, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 所撰《典章文物志》、《乙巳占》等書傳於世。

translations.literal: Books he wrote, such as the Dianzhang wenwu zhi and the Yisi zhan, have been handed down in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His works, including the Record of Institutions and Cultural Relics and the Yisi Divinations, circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子該，孫仙宗，並擢太史令。

translations.literal: His son Gai and grandson Xianzong were both promoted to Director of the Astronomical Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gai and grandson Xianzong both rose to Director of the Astronomical Bureau.

sentences.zh: 唐初言歷者惟傅仁均。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tang the one who spoke on calendars was only Fu Renjun.
translations.idiomatic: In early Tang, Fu Renjun alone dominated calendrical debate.

sentences.zh: 仁均，滑州人，終太史令。

translations.literal: Renjun was a man of Huazhou and ended as Director of the Astronomical Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Renjun came from Huazhou and ended his career as Director of the Astronomical Bureau.

sentences.zh: 甄權，許州扶溝人。

translations.literal: Zhen Quan was a native of Fugou in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen Quan was from Fugou in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 以母病，與弟立言究習方書，遂為高醫。

translations.literal: Because his mother was ill, he and his younger brother Liyan studied medical texts thoroughly and became eminent physicians.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, he and his younger brother Liyan threw themselves into medical texts and became celebrated physicians.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為秘書省正字，稱疾免。

translations.literal: He served the Sui as Proofreader of the Secretariat and pleaded illness to resign.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served as Proofreader in the Secretariat, then resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 魯州刺史庫狄嵚風痺不得挽弓，權使彀矢向堋立，鍼其肩隅，一進，曰：「可以射矣。」

translations.literal: The Prefect of Lu, Kudie Qin, had wind paralysis and could not draw a bow. Quan had him set arrows toward the butt and stand, needled the corner of his shoulder, withdrew once, and said, "You may shoot now."
translations.idiomatic: Kudie Qin, prefect of Lu, suffered wind paralysis and could not draw a bow. Quan had him stand with arrows nocked toward the target, inserted a needle at the corner of his shoulder, withdrew it once, and said, "You can shoot now."

sentences.zh: 果如言。

translations.literal: It turned out as he said.
translations.idiomatic: It proved exactly as he had said.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，權已百歲，太宗幸其舍，視飲食，訪逮其術，擢朝散大夫，賜幾杖衣服。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan, Quan was already a hundred; Taizong visited his house, observed his food and drink, inquired into his techniques, promoted him to Grand Master for Palace Leisure, and bestowed a staff, cane, and garments.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan, Quan was already a centenarian. Taizong visited his home, watched how he ate and drank, asked about his medical methods, promoted him to Grand Master for Palace Leisure, and granted him an honor staff, cane, and robes.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年一百三歲。

translations.literal: Soon after he died, aged one hundred three.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward, aged one hundred three.

sentences.zh: 所撰《脈經》、《針方》、《明堂》等圖傳於時。

translations.literal: Charts and books he compiled, such as the Maijing, Zhenfang, and Mingtang, circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His Pulse Classic, Acupuncture Formulas, Bright Hall diagrams, and related works circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 立言仕為太常丞。

translations.literal: Liyan served as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Liyan served as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 杜淹苦流腫，帝遣視，曰：「去此十日，午漏上，且死。」

translations.literal: Du Yan suffered severely from running sores; the emperor sent Liyan to examine him. He said, "Ten days from now, before the noon clepsydra mark, he will die."
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan was tormented by running sores; the emperor sent Liyan to examine him. He said, "In ten days, before the noon clepsydra stroke, he will die."

sentences.zh: 如之，有道人必腹懣煩彌二歲，診曰：「腹有蠱，誤食發而然。」

translations.literal: It was so. A certain Daoist had abdominal fullness and vexation for nearly two years; on examination he said, "There is gu in the belly—it came from mistakenly eating hair-triggering food."
translations.idiomatic: It happened as he predicted. A Daoist priest had suffered abdominal distension and distress for nearly two years. Liyan diagnosed him: "You have gu in the belly—caused by eating something that triggered it."

sentences.zh: 令餌雄黃一劑，少選，吐一蛇如拇，無目，燒之有發氣，乃愈。

translations.literal: He had him take one dose of realgar; after a little while he vomited a snake like a thumb, eyeless; when burned it gave off a hair-like odor, and he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He gave him one dose of realgar; shortly afterward the man vomited a thumb-sized, eyeless snake. When burned it smelled of hair, and he recovered.

sentences.zh: 後以醫顯者，清漳宋俠、義興許胤宗、洛陽張文仲李虔縱、京兆韋慈藏。

translations.literal: Later physicians who became famous were Song Xia of Qingzhang, Xu Yinzong of Yixing, Zhang Wenzong and Li Qianzong of Luoyang, and Wei Cizang of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Later physicians who won fame included Song Xia of Qingzhang, Xu Yinzong of Yixing, Zhang Wenzong and Li Qianzong of Luoyang, and Wei Cizang of the capital region.

sentences.zh: 俠官朝散大夫，藥藏監。

translations.literal: Xia held office as Grand Master for Palace Leisure and Superintendent of the Medicine Repository.
translations.idiomatic: Xia held the posts of Grand Master for Palace Leisure and Superintendent of the Medicine Repository.

sentences.zh: 胤宗仕陳為新蔡王外兵參軍。

translations.literal: Yinzong served Chen as External Troops Adjutant to the Prince of Xincai.
translations.idiomatic: Yinzong had served the Chen as External Troops Adjutant to the Prince of Xincai.

sentences.zh: 王太后病風不能言，脈沈難對，醫家告術窮。

translations.literal: The prince's mother fell ill with wind disease and could not speak; her pulse was deep and hard to match, and physicians declared their arts exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's mother suffered a wind ailment and could not speak; her pulse was deep and baffling, and other physicians declared themselves at a loss.

sentences.zh: 胤宗曰：「餌液不可進。」

translations.literal: Yinzong said, "Oral medicines cannot be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Yinzong said, "She cannot take medicine by mouth."

sentences.zh: 即以黃耆、防風煮湯數十斛，置床下，氣如霧，熏薄之，是夕語。

translations.literal: He then boiled dozens of hu of decoction of astragalus and saposhnikovia, placed it beneath the bed, let the vapor rise like mist, and fumigated her thinly; that evening she spoke.
translations.idiomatic: He boiled dozens of hu of astragalus and saposhnikovia decoction, set the vessels under her bed so the steam rose like mist, and let the fumes bathe her—by evening she could speak again.

sentences.zh: 擢義興太守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Prefect of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 武德初，累進散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he was repeatedly advanced to Attendant Cavalier.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude era he rose step by step to Attendant Cavalier.

sentences.zh: 關中多骨蒸疾，轉相染，得者皆死，胤宗療視必愈。

translations.literal: In Guanzhong bone-steaming disease was widespread and passed from one to another; those who caught it all died, yet whenever Yinzong treated and examined them they recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Bone-steaming fever ravaged Guanzhong, spreading contagiously and killing nearly everyone who contracted it—yet Yinzong's patients invariably recovered.

sentences.zh: 或勸其著書貽後世者，答曰：「醫特意耳，思慮精則得之。

translations.literal: Some urged him to write books for posterity; he answered, "Medicine lies in focused intent—when thought is refined one obtains it.
translations.idiomatic: When others urged him to write for posterity, he replied, "Medicine depends on focused insight—refine your thinking and you grasp it.

sentences.zh: 脈之候幽而難明，吾意所解，口莫能宣也。

translations.literal: The signs of the pulse are hidden and hard to clarify; what my mind understands my mouth cannot declare.
translations.idiomatic: Pulse signs are subtle and elusive; what I understand in the mind, words cannot convey.

sentences.zh: 古之上醫，要在視脈，病乃可識。

translations.literal: The superior physicians of antiquity lay chiefly in viewing the pulse—only then could illness be recognized.
translations.idiomatic: The great physicians of antiquity relied above all on reading the pulse; only then could disease be truly known.

sentences.zh: 病與藥值，唯用一物攻之，氣純而愈速。

translations.literal: When disease and drug match, use only one thing to attack it—the qi is pure and recovery is swift.
translations.idiomatic: When illness and remedy align, use a single drug to strike at it—its force stays pure and recovery comes quickly.

sentences.zh: 今之人不善為脈，以情度病，多其物以幸有功，譬獵不知兔，廣絡原野，冀一人獲之，術亦疏矣。

translations.literal: People today are poor at taking the pulse; they gauge disease by feeling and multiply drugs hoping for merit—as if hunting without knowing where the rabbit is, spreading nets across the whole wild, hoping one man will catch it: the technique is crude indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Today's doctors cannot read pulses well; they guess at disease by mood and pile on drugs hoping something works—like hunting without knowing where the rabbit lies, casting nets across the whole plain and hoping someone catches one. That is crude practice.

sentences.zh: 一藥偶得，它味相制，弗能專力，此難愈之驗也。

translations.literal: One drug may happen to fit, but other flavors restrain one another and cannot concentrate force—this is proof of why recovery is hard.
translations.idiomatic: One ingredient may suit the case, yet other flavors counteract it and blunt its power—that is why cures fail.

sentences.zh: 脈之妙處不可傳，虛著方劑，終無益於世，此吾所以不著書也。」

translations.literal: The subtle points of the pulse cannot be transmitted; to write formulas in vain ultimately benefits the world not at all—this is why I do not write books."
translations.idiomatic: The subtle art of the pulse cannot be handed down; empty prescription books would help no one. That is why I refuse to publish."

sentences.zh: 卒年七十餘。

translations.literal: He died aged over seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his seventies.

sentences.zh: 文仲仕武後時，至尚藥奉禦。

translations.literal: Wenzong served in Empress Wu's time and reached Attending Physician of Imperial Medicines.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong served under Empress Wu and rose to Attending Physician of Imperial Medicines.

sentences.zh: 特進蘇良嗣方朝，疾作，仆廷中。

translations.literal: Special Advancement Holder Su Liangsi was at court when his illness struck and he collapsed in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Special Advancement Holder Su Liangsi was at court when he was seized by illness and collapsed in the hall.

sentences.zh: 文仲診曰：「憂憤而成，若脅痛者，殆未可救。」

translations.literal: Wenzong diagnosed him and said, "It was formed from worry and anger; if flank pain appears, he will probably not be saved."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong examined him and said, "This arose from worry and anger. If flank pain sets in, he will likely not survive."

sentences.zh: 頃告脅痛。

translations.literal: Shortly he reported flank pain.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he complained of flank pain.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「及心則貽。」

translations.literal: He also said, "When it reaches the heart it will be fatal."
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong added, "When it reaches the heart, he is lost."

sentences.zh: 俄心痛而死。

translations.literal: Soon heart pain came and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon heart pain seized him and he died.

sentences.zh: 文仲論風與氣尤精。

translations.literal: Wenzong's discourse on wind and qi was especially refined.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong's understanding of wind and qi disorders was especially keen.

sentences.zh: 後集諸言方者與共著書，詔王方慶監之。

translations.literal: Later those who spoke of formulas were gathered to compile books together, and Wang Fangqing was ordered to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: Later the court gathered leading formula physicians to compile medical books under Wang Fangqing's supervision.

sentences.zh: 文仲曰：「風狀百二十四，氣狀八十，治不以時，則死及之。

translations.literal: Wenzong said, "Wind conditions number one hundred twenty-four, qi conditions eighty; if treatment is not timely, death overtakes one.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong said, "There are one hundred twenty-four patterns of wind disease and eighty of qi disorder. Treat them out of season and death follows.

sentences.zh: 惟頭風與上氣、足氣，藥可常禦。

translations.literal: Only head-wind, upper qi, and foot qi can be regularly warded off with drugs.
translations.idiomatic: Only head-wind, upper qi, and foot qi can be held at bay with regular medication.

sentences.zh: 病風之人，春秋末月，可使洞利，乃不困劇，自餘須發則治，以時消息。」

translations.literal: For those ill with wind, in the last months of spring and autumn one may give strong purgation so they are not distressed severely; for the rest, treat when it flares and let it subside with the seasons."
translations.idiomatic: For wind patients, give a strong purge in the last month of spring or autumn to spare them severe attacks; otherwise treat only when symptoms flare, following seasonal rhythms."

sentences.zh: 乃著《四時輕重術》凡十八種上之。

translations.literal: He then compiled the Sishi qingzhong shu in eighteen categories and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted his Treatise on Seasonal Severity in Medicine in eighteen categories.

sentences.zh: 虔縱官侍禦醫，慈藏光祿卿。

translations.literal: Qianzong held office as Attending Imperial Physician; Cizang was Grand Master for the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Qianzong served as Attending Imperial Physician; Cizang held the rank of Grand Master for the Palace.

sentences.zh: 袁天綱，益州成都人。

translations.literal: Yuan Tiangang was a native of Chengdu in Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Tiangang came from Chengdu in Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 仕隋為鹽官令。

translations.literal: He served the Sui as Magistrate of Yanguan.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui he served as magistrate of Yanguan.

sentences.zh: 仕隨為鹽官令。

translations.literal: He served Sui as Magistrate of Yanguan.
translations.idiomatic: He likewise served the Sui as magistrate of Yanguan.

sentences.zh: 在洛陽，與杜淹、王珪、韋挺遊，天綱謂淹曰：「公蘭臺、學堂全且博，將以文章顯。」

translations.literal: In Luoyang he associated with Du Yan, Wang Gui, and Wei Ting. Tiangang said to Yan, "Your Orchid Terrace and Study Hall are complete and broad; you will become famous through literature."
translations.idiomatic: In Luoyang he befriended Du Yan, Wang Gui, and Wei Ting. Tiangang told Yan, "Your Orchid Terrace and Study Hall marks are full and broad—you will win fame through writing."

sentences.zh: 謂珪「法令成，天地相臨，不十年官五品」；

translations.literal: To Gui he said, "Your decree lines are formed; heaven and earth face each other—within ten years you will reach fifth rank";
translations.idiomatic: To Gui he said, "Your decree lines are set; heaven and earth press upon you—in less than ten years you will reach fifth rank";

sentences.zh: 謂挺「面如虎，當以武處官」；

translations.literal: to Ting he said, "Your face is like a tiger's—you should gain office through martial means";
translations.idiomatic: to Ting, "Your face is tiger-like—you will rise through military office";

sentences.zh: 「然三君久皆得譴，吾且見之」。

translations.literal: "yet all three of you gentlemen will in time suffer dismissal—I shall yet see it."
translations.idiomatic: "yet all three of you will eventually suffer dismissal—and I shall live to see it."

sentences.zh: 淹以侍御史入天策為學士，珪太子中允，挺善隱太子，薦為左衛率。

translations.literal: Yan entered the Heavenly Stratagem Academy as Academician through his post as Attending Censor; Gui was Crown Prince's Principal; Ting was intimate with the Hidden Crown Prince and was recommended as Left Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Yan entered the Heavenly Stratagem Academy as academician from his post as attending censor; Gui became principal of the crown prince's household; Ting, close to the hidden crown prince, was recommended as Left Guard General.

sentences.zh: 武德中，俱以事流雋州，見天綱，曰：「公等終且貴。

translations.literal: In Wude all were banished to Jun prefecture for their affairs; they met Tiangang, who said, "You gentlemen will in the end still be noble.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude all three were exiled to Jun prefecture over political troubles. Meeting Tiangang again, they heard him say, "You will still rise to wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 杜位三品，難與言壽，王、韋亦三品，後於杜而壽過之，但晚節皆困。」

translations.literal: Du will reach third rank—it is hard to speak of his lifespan. Wang and Wei will also reach third rank, later than Du but living longer than he; yet all will be distressed in their late years."
translations.idiomatic: Du will reach third rank, though I cannot speak confidently of his lifespan. Wang and Wei will also reach third rank, later than Du but outliving him—yet all three will suffer hardship in their final years."

sentences.zh: 見竇軌曰：「君伏犀貫玉枕，輔角完起，十年且顯，立功其在梁、益間邪！」

translations.literal: Meeting Dou Gui he said, "My lord, your hidden rhinoceros runs through the jade pillow, your cheek angles rise complete—in ten years you will be eminent; your merit will be between Liang and Yi, will it not!"
translations.idiomatic: Meeting Dou Gui he said, "Your hidden-rhinoceros mark runs through the jade-pillow zone and your cheek angles stand full—in ten years you will shine; your achievements will lie between Liang and Yi, will they not!"

sentences.zh: 軌後為益州行臺仆射，天綱復曰：「赤脈幹瞳，方語而浮赤入大宅，公為將必多殺，願自戒。」

translations.literal: Later Gui became Regional Commander of Yizhou; Tiangang again said, "Red vessels dry the pupils; as you speak, floating red enters the great mansion—as a general you will surely kill many; I wish you would warn yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Gui became regional commander of Yizhou, Tiangang warned again: "Red vessels streak your pupils; even as you speak, red qi floods the great mansion—as a commander you will slaughter many. Guard yourself."

sentences.zh: 軌果坐事見召。

translations.literal: Gui indeed was summoned because of an affair.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was indeed summoned to court over a legal matter.

sentences.zh: 天綱曰：「公毋憂，右輔澤而動，不久必還。」

translations.literal: Tiangang said, "My lord, do not worry—the right assistant is moist and stirring; before long you will surely return."
translations.idiomatic: Tiangang told him, "Do not worry—your right assistant zone is moist and active; you will return soon."

sentences.zh: 果還為都督。

translations.literal: He did return as regional inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He was indeed restored as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，太宗召見曰：「古有君平，朕今得爾，何如？」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan Taizong summoned him and said, "In antiquity there was Junping; today I have obtained you—how does that compare?"
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan, Taizong received him and said, "Ancient times had Yan Junping; now I have you—how do we compare?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「彼不逢時，臣固勝之。」

translations.literal: He replied, "He did not meet his time; your subject is surely superior to him."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "He missed his age; your servant is certainly the better fortune."

sentences.zh: 武後之幼，天綱見其母曰：「夫人法生貴子。」

translations.literal: When Empress Wu was young, Tiangang saw her mother and said, "Madam, by physiognomy you will bear noble sons."
translations.idiomatic: When the future Empress Wu was still a girl, Tiangang met her mother and said, "Madam, your features promise noble sons."

sentences.zh: 乃見二子元慶、元爽，曰：「官三品，保家主也。」

translations.literal: He then saw her two sons Yuangqing and Yuanshuang and said, "Third-rank offices—they are masters who preserve the family."
translations.idiomatic: He then examined her sons Yuangqing and Yuanshuang: "Third rank—men who will uphold the household."

sentences.zh: 見韓國夫人，曰：「此女貴而不利夫。」

translations.literal: Seeing the Lady of Han he said, "This daughter is noble but not favorable to her husband."
translations.idiomatic: Of the Lady of Han he said, "This daughter will be exalted but bring her husband no good."

sentences.zh: 後最幼，姆抱以見，紿以男，天綱視其步與目，驚曰：「龍瞳鳳頸，極貴驗也；

translations.literal: The youngest, Wu, was brought in her nurse's arms; they deceived him that she was a boy. Tiangang looked at her gait and eyes and cried in alarm, "Dragon pupils and phoenix neck—the utmost signs of nobility;
translations.idiomatic: The youngest girl was carried in by her nurse, passed off as a boy. Tiangang studied her gait and eyes and exclaimed, "Dragon pupils and a phoenix neck—the highest marks of eminence;

sentences.zh: 若為女，當作天子。」

translations.literal: if she were a woman, she would become Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: if this child were a girl, she would become Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 帝在九成宮，令視岑文本，曰：「學堂瑩夷，眉過目，故文章振天下。

translations.literal: The emperor was at Jiucheng Palace and had him view Cen Wende, saying, "The Study Hall is bright and level, the brows pass the eyes—therefore his writings shake the realm.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiucheng Palace the emperor had him examine Cen Wende. Tiangang said, "His Study Hall is luminous and even, his brows overshoot his eyes—hence his prose shook the empire.

sentences.zh: 首生骨未成，自前而視，法三品。

translations.literal: The bone at the crown of the head is not yet formed; viewed from the front, by rule he is third rank.
translations.idiomatic: The crown bone is not yet fully formed; viewed from the front, his marks fit third rank.

sentences.zh: 肉不稱骨，非壽兆也。」

translations.literal: Flesh does not match bone—this is not a sign of long life."
translations.idiomatic: His flesh does not match his bone structure—not a sign of long life."

sentences.zh: 張行成、馬周見，曰：「馬君伏犀貫腦，背若有負，貴驗也。

translations.literal: Seeing Zhang Xingcheng and Ma Zhou he said, "Master Ma's hidden rhinoceros runs through the brain, his back as if bearing a load—signs of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: Examining Zhang Xingcheng and Ma Zhou, he said of Ma, "The hidden-rhinoceros mark runs through his brain, his back as though carrying a burden—marks of high rank.

sentences.zh: 近古君臣相遇未有及公者。

translations.literal: In recent antiquity the meeting of ruler and minister has never equaled yours.
translations.idiomatic: In recent times no bond between ruler and minister has matched what awaits you.

sentences.zh: 然面澤赤而耳無根，後骨不隆，壽不長也。

translations.literal: Yet the face is moist and red while the ears have no root, the back of the skull does not rise—life will not be long.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his face is flushed and ruddy, his ears lack deep roots, and the back of his skull does not rise—he will not live long.

sentences.zh: 張晚得官，終位宰相。」

translations.literal: Zhang obtained office late and in the end reached the rank of chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang rose to office late but ended as chief minister."

sentences.zh: 其術精類如此。

translations.literal: His art's refinement was of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His craft was uncannily precise in just this way.

sentences.zh: 高士廉曰：「君終作何官？」

translations.literal: Gao Shilian said, "What office will you finally hold?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shilian asked him, "What post will you hold in the end?"

sentences.zh: 謝曰：「仆及夏四月，數既盡。」

translations.literal: He declined, saying, "Your servant will reach the fourth month of summer, and his number is already exhausted."
translations.idiomatic: He demurred: "I will last only until the fourth month of summer—my allotted span is finished."

sentences.zh: 如期以火山令卒。

translations.literal: On schedule he died as Magistrate of Huoshan.
translations.idiomatic: He died on schedule while serving as magistrate of Huoshan.

sentences.zh: 子客師，亦傳其術，為廩犧令。

translations.literal: His son Keshi also transmitted his art and served as Magistrate of Grain and Sacrificial Animals.
translations.idiomatic: His son Keshi inherited his methods and served as magistrate of the grain and sacrificial-animal office.

sentences.zh: 高宗置一鼠於奩，令術家射，皆曰鼠。

translations.literal: Gaozong placed a mouse in a casket and had technicians divine it; all said it was a mouse.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong hid a mouse in a casket and asked diviners to identify it; all declared it a mouse.

sentences.zh: 客師獨曰：「強實鼠，然入則一，出則四。」

translations.literal: Keshi alone said, "It is certainly a mouse, yet going in there was one, coming out there will be four."
translations.idiomatic: Keshi alone said, "It is indeed a mouse—but one went in and four will come out."

sentences.zh: 發之，鼠生三子。

translations.literal: When they opened it, the mouse had borne three young.
translations.idiomatic: When they opened the casket, the mouse had just given birth to three pups.

sentences.zh: 嘗度江，叩舟而還，左右請故，曰：「舟中人鼻下氣皆墨，不可以濟。」

translations.literal: Once crossing the river he knocked on the boat and turned back; his attendants asked the reason. He said, "The breath below the noses of those in the boat is all black—they cannot be crossed with."
translations.idiomatic: Once, about to cross a river, he struck the boat and turned back. When attendants asked why, he said, "Everyone aboard has black qi beneath the nose—we cannot sail with them."

sentences.zh: 俄有一男子，跛而負，直就舟，客師曰：「貴人在，吾可以濟。」

translations.literal: Soon a man came, lame and carrying a load, and went straight onto the boat. Keshi said, "A noble man is present—we may cross."
translations.idiomatic: Soon a lame man carrying a load boarded directly. Keshi said, "A man of rank is here—we may cross now."

sentences.zh: 江中風忽起，幾覆而免。

translations.literal: Wind suddenly rose on the river and they were nearly capsized but escaped.
translations.idiomatic: A sudden gale nearly swamped them, yet they escaped.

sentences.zh: 跛男子乃婁師德也。

translations.literal: The lame man was Lou Shide.
translations.idiomatic: The lame man was Lou Shide.

sentences.zh: 時有長社人張憬藏，持與天綱埒。

translations.literal: At the time there was Zhang Jingzang of Changshe, held equal to Tiangang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Jingzang of Changshe was considered Tiangang's equal.

sentences.zh: 太子詹事蔣儼有所問，答曰：「公厄在三尺土下，盡六年而貴，六十位蒲州刺史，無有祿矣。」

translations.literal: Jiang Yan, Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household, had a question; he answered, "Your lordship's calamity lies beneath three chi of earth; in full six years you will be noble; at sixty you will hold Puzhou prefecture and have no salary."
translations.idiomatic: When Jiang Yan, steward of the heir apparent's household, consulted him, he answered, "Your ordeal lies under three feet of earth. In six full years you will rise; at sixty you will be prefect of Puzhou—and receive no salary."

sentences.zh: 儼使高麗，為莫離支所囚，居土室六年還。

translations.literal: Yan was sent to Goguryeo, imprisoned by the Molichi, and dwelt in an earthen cell six years before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was sent to Goguryeo, imprisoned by the Molichi, and spent six years in an earthen cell before returning.

sentences.zh: 及為蒲州，歲如期，則召掾史、妻子，告當死，俄詔聽致仕。

translations.literal: When he became prefect of Puzhou, in the year as predicted he summoned clerks and wife, announced he was about to die, and soon an edict allowed him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Puzhou, when the predicted year came he gathered clerks and family, announced his death was near—and soon received permission to retire.

sentences.zh: 劉仁軌與鄉人靖賢請占，憬藏答曰：「劉公當五品而譴，終位冠人臣。」

translations.literal: Liu Ren'gui and his fellow villager Jing Xian asked for a reading; Jingzang answered, "Master Liu will reach fifth rank and suffer dismissal, yet in the end his position will crown all ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ren'gui and his neighbor Jing Xian sought a reading. Jingzang said, "Liu will reach fifth rank and face dismissal, yet in the end he will stand above all ministers."

sentences.zh: 謂賢曰：「君法客死。」

translations.literal: To Xian he said, "By your physiognomy you will die away from home."
translations.idiomatic: To Xian he said, "Your features mark you for death far from home."

sentences.zh: 仁軌為尚書仆射。

translations.literal: Ren'gui became Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ren'gui became Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 賢猥曰：「我三子皆富田宅，吾何客死？」

translations.literal: Xian rudely said, "My three sons all have rich fields and houses—why should I die away from home?"
translations.idiomatic: Xian scoffed, "My three sons all own rich estates—why should I die abroad?"

sentences.zh: 俄喪三子，盡鬻田宅，寄死友家。

translations.literal: Soon he lost all three sons, sold every field and house, and lodged his death at a friend's home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon all three sons died; he sold every field and house and died as a guest in a friend's home.

sentences.zh: 魏元忠尚少，往見憬藏，問之，久不答，元忠怒曰：「窮通有命，何預君邪？」

translations.literal: Wei Yuanzhong was still young and went to see Jingzang to ask; for long he did not answer. Yuanzhong angrily said, "Poverty and success have fate—what has it to do with you?"
translations.idiomatic: Wei Yuanzhong, still young, visited Jingzang for a reading, but Jingzang was silent so long that Yuanzhong snapped, "Fortune and ruin are fated—what business is it of yours?"

sentences.zh: 拂衣去。

translations.literal: He brushed his robe and left.
translations.idiomatic: He brushed off his sleeves and walked out.

sentences.zh: 憬藏遽起曰：「君之相在怒時，位必卿相。」

translations.literal: Jingzang rose hastily and said, "Your lordship's physiognomy lies in your moment of anger—your rank will surely be minister or chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: Jingzang sprang up and cried, "Your physiognomy shows best in anger—you are fated for the highest ministerial rank."

sentences.zh: 姚崇、李迥秀、杜景佺往從之遊，憬藏曰：「三人者皆宰相，然姚最貴。」

translations.literal: Yao Chong, Li Huijiu, and Du Jingqian went to associate with him; Jingzang said, "All three will be chancellors, yet Yao is the most exalted."
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chong, Li Huijiu, and Du Jingqian came to study with him, Jingzang said, "All three will become chancellors—but Yao will rank highest."

sentences.zh: 郎中裴珪妻趙見之，憬藏曰：「夫人目修緩，法曰『豕視淫』，又曰『目有四白，五夫守宅』，夫人且得罪。」

translations.literal: The wife Zhao of Bureau Director Pei Gui came to see him; Jingzang said, "Madam, your eyes are long and slow; by rule this is 'pig-gaze lewdness,' and also 'eyes with four whites—five husbands guard the house.' Madam will soon offend."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Gui's wife Zhao consulted him. Jingzang said, "Your eyes are long and languid—the texts call this 'swinish, lustful gaze,' and also 'four whites in the eye—five husbands guarding the house.' Madam, you will soon fall into disgrace."

sentences.zh: 俄坐奸，沒入掖廷。

translations.literal: Soon she was convicted of adultery and confiscated into the palace women's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Soon she was convicted of adultery and sent to the palace women's quarters.

sentences.zh: 裴光廷當國，憬藏以紙大署「臺」字投之，光廷曰：「吾既臺司矣，尚何事？」

translations.literal: Pei Guangting held state power; Jingzang wrote large on paper the character "Tai" and tossed it to him. Guangting said, "I am already head of the Secretariat—what else is there?"
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Guangting dominated the government, Jingzang tossed him a slip bearing the character "Tai." Guangting said, "I already head the secretariat—what more could you mean?"

sentences.zh: 後三日，貶臺州刺史。

translations.literal: Three days later he was demoted to Prefect of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later he was demoted to prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 隋末又有高唐人乙弗弘禮，當煬帝居藩，召見，弘禮賀曰：「大王為萬乘主，所戒在德而已。」

translations.literal: At the end of Sui there was also Yifu Hongli of Gaotang. When Emperor Yang was still in his princely residence he was summoned and received; Hongli congratulated him, saying, "Great King, you will be lord of ten thousand chariots; what you must guard is virtue alone."
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Sui there was also Yifu Hongli of Gaotang. When Yang Di was still prince, Hongli was summoned and congratulated him: "Your Highness will rule the realm—the only warning is to keep your virtue."

sentences.zh: 及即位，悉詔諸術家坊處之，使弘禮總攝。

translations.literal: When he took the throne he summoned all technicians to one ward and had Hongli supervise them in general.
translations.idiomatic: On his accession he gathered all occult specialists into one ward and put Hongli in overall charge.

sentences.zh: 海內浸亂，帝曰：「而昔言朕既驗，然終當奈何？」

translations.literal: As the realm grew ever more chaotic the emperor said, "Your words of old about me have been verified—yet what will be the end?"
translations.idiomatic: As the empire slid into chaos the emperor said, "Your prophecy about me has come true—so what becomes of me in the end?"

sentences.zh: 弘禮逡巡，帝知之，乃曰：「不言，且死！」

translations.literal: Hongli hesitated; the emperor knew it and said, "If you do not speak, you will die for it!"
translations.idiomatic: Hongli hesitated. The emperor understood and snapped, "Speak—or die!"

sentences.zh: 弘禮曰：「臣觀人臣相與陛下類者不長，然聖人不相，故臣不能知。」

translations.literal: Hongli said, "Your servant observes that subjects whose physiognomy resembles Your Majesty's does not live long; yet the sage is not physiognomized, so your servant cannot know."
translations.idiomatic: Hongli said, "I see that ministers who resemble your majesty in physiognomy do not live long—but the sage cannot be read by such arts, so I cannot tell your fate."

sentences.zh: 由是敕有司監視，毋得與外語。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the relevant offices to watch him and forbid speech with outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered officials to guard him and forbid contact with outsiders.

sentences.zh: 薛大鼎坐事沒為奴，及貞觀時，有請於弘禮，答曰：「君，奴也，欲何事？」

translations.literal: Xue Dading was enslaved for an offense; in Zhenguan times he made a request of Hongli, who answered, "You, sir, are a slave—what do you want?"
translations.idiomatic: Xue Dading had been enslaved for a crime. In the Zhenguan era he consulted Hongli, who replied, "You are a slave—what do you want from me?"

sentences.zh: 請解衣視之，弘禮指腰而下曰：「位方嶽。」

translations.literal: He asked to strip and be examined; Hongli pointed from the waist downward and said, "Rank of a regional lord."
translations.idiomatic: He asked Hongli to examine him bare-bodied. Hongli pointed from the waist down and said, "You are marked for a regional lord's rank."

sentences.zh: 玄宗時有金梁鳳者，頗言人貴賤夭壽。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xuanzong's time there was Jin Liangfeng, who often spoke of men's noble or base rank and early or late death.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanzong there was Jin Liangfeng, famed for predicting men's rank and lifespan.

sentences.zh: 裴冕為河西留後，梁鳳輒言：「不半歲兵起，君當以御史中丞除宰相。」

translations.literal: Pei Mian was military commissioner of Hexi; Liangfeng often said, "Within half a year war will rise; you will be removed from office as Vice Censor-in-Chief and made chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Mian was military commissioner of Hexi, Liangfeng kept saying, "War will break out within half a year. You will leave office as vice censor-in-chief and become chancellor."

sentences.zh: 又言：「一日向雒，一日向蜀，一日向朔方，此時公當國。」

translations.literal: He also said, "One day toward Luoyang, one day toward Shu, one day toward Shuofang—at that time you will hold the state."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "One day you will face Luoyang, one day Shu, one day Shuofang—and then you will hold the realm."

sentences.zh: 冕妖其言，絕之。

translations.literal: Mian thought his words demonic and cut off contact.
translations.idiomatic: Mian found his words uncanny and broke off contact.

sentences.zh: 俄而祿山反，冕以御史中丞召，因問三日，答曰：「雒日即滅，蜀日不能久，朔方日愈明。」

translations.literal: Soon An Lushan rebelled; Mian was summoned as Vice Censor-in-Chief and therefore asked about the three days. He answered, "The Luoyang day will be extinguished at once, the Shu day cannot last long, the Shuofang day grows ever brighter."
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Mian was summoned as vice censor-in-chief and asked about the three days. Liangfeng answered, "The Luoyang day dies quickly, the Shu day cannot endure, the Shuofang day grows brighter."

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，而冕遂相，薦於帝，拜都水使者。

translations.literal: Suzong took the throne and Mian became chancellor, recommended him to the emperor, and he was appointed Commissioner of the Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzong took the throne Mian became chancellor, recommended Liangfeng, and the emperor appointed him Commissioner of the Waterways.

sentences.zh: 梁鳳謂呂諲曰：「君且輔政，須大怖乃得。」

translations.literal: Liangfeng said to Lv Jin, "You will soon assist in government, but you must suffer great terror first."
translations.idiomatic: Liangfeng told Lv Jin, "You will soon join the government—but only after a great fright."

sentences.zh: 諲責驛史，之，史突入射諲，兩矢風中，走而免，明年知政事。

translations.literal: Jin blamed a postal clerk and went to him; the clerk burst in and shot at Jin—two arrows caught in the wind—and he fled and escaped; the next year he entered the administration.
translations.idiomatic: Jin rebuked a courier, who ambushed him and shot twice—both arrows were blown off course—and Jin fled unharmed. The next year he entered the chief council.

sentences.zh: 李揆、盧允毀服紿謁，梁鳳不許，二人語以情，梁鳳曰：「李自舍人閱歲而相，盧不過郎官。」

translations.literal: Li Kui and Lu Yun destroyed their dress and deceptively called on him; Liangfeng would not receive them. The two spoke of their feelings; Liangfeng said, "Li from Reviewer will be chancellor within a year; Lu will not pass Bureau Director."
translations.idiomatic: Li Kui and Lu Yun came in mourning garb on a pretext, but Liangfeng refused them. When they pleaded, he said, "Li will be chancellor within a year from his reviewer post; Lu will rise no higher than bureau director."

sentences.zh: 揆已相，擢允吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Kui was already chancellor and promoted Yun to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Kui became chancellor he promoted Yun to bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 王遠知，系本瑯邪，後為揚州人。

translations.literal: Wang Yuanzhi's clan origin was Langya, but later he was a man of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuanzhi's lineage traced to Langya, though he later lived as a native of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父曇選，為陳揚州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Tanxuan served Chen as Prefect of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tanxuan had been prefect of Yangzhou under Chen.

sentences.zh: 母晝寢，夢鳳集其身，因有娠。

translations.literal: His mother napped by day, dreamed a phoenix gathered on her body, and thus became pregnant.
translations.idiomatic: His mother dreamed during a daytime nap that a phoenix alighted on her, and she conceived.

sentences.zh: 浮屠寶誌謂曇選曰：「生子當為世方士。」

translations.literal: The monk Baozhi told Tanxuan, "The son born will be a fangshi of the age."
translations.idiomatic: The monk Baozhi told Tanxuan, "Your son will become a master of occult arts for his generation."

sentences.zh: 遠知少警敏，多通書傳，事陶弘景，傳其術，為道士。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi in youth was alert and keen, mastered many books and records, served Tao Hongjing and received his arts, and became a Daoist priest.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi was clever and quick as a youth, read widely, studied under Tao Hongjing, inherited his methods, and became a Daoist priest.

sentences.zh: 又從臧兢遊。

translations.literal: He also associated with Zang Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He also studied with Zang Jing.

sentences.zh: 陳後主聞其名，召入重陽殿，辯論超詣，甚見咨挹。

translations.literal: Chen Houzhu heard his name and summoned him into the Chongyang Hall; his disputation was surpassing and he was greatly consulted and esteemed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Houzhu of Chen summoned him to the Chongyang Hall after hearing his fame; his discourse was extraordinary and won deep respect.

sentences.zh: 隋煬帝為晉王，鎮揚州，使人介以邀見，少選發白，俄復鬢，帝懼，遣之。

translations.literal: When Sui Emperor Yang was Prince of Jin and stationed at Yangzhou he sent an intermediary to invite him; after a little while his hair turned white, then soon black again at the temples—the emperor was afraid and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Di was Prince of Jin at Yangzhou he sent for him; Yuanzhi's hair briefly turned white, then black again at the temples. The prince was alarmed and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 後幸涿郡，詔遠知見臨朔宮，帝執弟子禮，咨質仙事，詔京師作玉清玄壇以處之。

translations.literal: Later when he visited Zhuo command he ordered Yuanzhi to meet him at Linshuo Palace; the emperor performed the disciple's rite, consulted on immortal matters, and ordered the capital to build a Jade Pure Mysterious Altar to house him.
translations.idiomatic: On a later visit to Zhuo he received Yuanzhi at Linshuo Palace, treated him as a disciple, questioned him on immortality, and ordered a Jade Pure altar built in the capital for his residence.

sentences.zh: 及幸揚州，遠知謂帝不宜遠京國，不省。

translations.literal: When he visited Yangzhou, Yuanzhi told the emperor he should not go far from the capital region; he did not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured Yangzhou, Yuanzhi warned that he should not stray far from the capital—but was ignored.

sentences.zh: 高祖尚微，遠知密語天命。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was still obscure, Yuanzhi spoke secretly of the Mandate of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu was still unknown, Yuanzhi confided to him about the Mandate of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 武德中，平王世充，秦王與房玄齡微服過之，遠知未識，迎語曰：「中有聖人，非王乎？」

translations.literal: In Wude, after pacifying Wang Shichong, the Prince of Qin and Fang Xuanling passed in plain dress; Yuanzhi did not recognize them and greeted them, saying, "Among you is a sage—is it not the prince?"
translations.idiomatic: During Wude, after the defeat of Wang Shichong, the Prince of Qin and Fang Xuanling visited in disguise. Yuanzhi did not recognize them but said, "There is a sage among you—is it not the prince?"

sentences.zh: 乃念以寶。

translations.literal: They then intoned his name and presented a precious tally as proof.
translations.idiomatic: They then spoke his name and showed a precious tally to prove their identity.

sentences.zh: 遠知曰：「方為太平天子，願自愛。」

translations.literal: Yuanzhi said, "You are about to become the Son of Heaven in an age of peace—take care of yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi said, "You are about to become Son of Heaven in an age of peace—guard yourself well."

sentences.zh: 太宗立，欲官之，苦辭。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne he wished to give him office, but he adamantly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne he wished to appoint him, but Yuanzhi firmly refused office.

sentences.zh: 貞觀九年，詔潤州即茆山為觀，俾居之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenguan an edict ordered Runzhou to establish Maoshan as an abbey for him to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year nine he was ordered to dwell at an abbey established on Maoshan in Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 璽詔曰：「省所奏，願還舊山，已別詔不違雅素，並敕立祠觀，以伸曩懷。

translations.literal: An imperial edict said, "We have reviewed your memorial wishing to return to your old mountain; a separate edict already does not violate your refined plainness, and we also order a shrine-abbey established to fulfill your long-held wish.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict read: "We have read your request to return to your old mountain. A separate order will respect your plain ways, and we command a shrine-abbey built to fulfill your long-held wish.

sentences.zh: 未知先生早晚至江外，祠舍何當就功？

translations.literal: We do not know when the master will arrive south of the river, or when the shrine buildings will be completed.
translations.idiomatic: We do not know when you will come south of the Yangzi, or when the shrine will be finished.

sentences.zh: 令太史令薛頤等往宣朕意。」

translations.literal: We order Director of the Astronomical Bureau Xue Yi and others to go announce Our intent."
translations.idiomatic: We send Director of the Astronomical Bureau Xue Yi and others to convey our wishes."

sentences.zh: 遠知多怪言，詫其弟子潘師正曰：「吾少也有累，不得上天，今署少室伯，吾將行。」

translations.literal: Yuanzhi had many strange sayings; he told his disciple Pan Shizheng in wonder, "In my youth I had burdens and could not ascend to heaven; now I am appointed Baron of Lesser Chamber—I am about to go."
translations.idiomatic: Yuanzhi spoke many uncanny things. He told his disciple Pan Shizheng, "In youth I carried burdens and could not ascend heaven. Now I am appointed Baron of Lesser Chamber—I am leaving."

sentences.zh: 即沐浴，加冠衣，若寢者，遂卒。

translations.literal: He then bathed, put on cap and robes as if to sleep, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He bathed, donned cap and robes as if for sleep, and died.

sentences.zh: 或言壽蓋百二十六歲雲。

translations.literal: Some say his lifespan was about one hundred twenty-six years.
translations.idiomatic: Some said he lived about one hundred twenty-six years.

sentences.zh: 遺命子紹業曰：「爾年六十五見天子，七十見女君。」

translations.literal: He left instructions to his son Shaoye: "At sixty-five you will see the Son of Heaven; at seventy you will see the female sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: He told his son Shaoye, "At sixty-five you will see the Son of Heaven; at seventy you will see the female sovereign."

sentences.zh: 調露中，紹業表其言，高宗召見，嗟賞，追贈遠知太中大夫，謚升真先生。

translations.literal: In Tiaolu, Shaoye memorialized his words; Gaozong summoned and praised him, posthumously enfeoffing Yuanzhi as Grand Master for Palace Grandee with posthumous title Master of Ascended Truth.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiaolu, Shaoye reported these words to the throne. Gaozong summoned him, admired the prophecy, and posthumously honored Yuanzhi as Grand Master for Palace Grandee with the posthumous title Master of Ascended Truth.

sentences.zh: 武後時復召見，皆如其年。

translations.literal: In Wu Hou's time he was again summoned and received—all as predicted by age.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he was summoned again—exactly at the ages foretold.

sentences.zh: 又贈金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was again granted Golden Purple Glory Grand Master for the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was again granted the rank of Golden Purple Glory Grand Master for the Palace.

sentences.zh: 天授中改謚升玄。

translations.literal: In Tianshou his posthumous name was changed to Ascended Mystery.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianshou era his posthumous title was changed to Master of Ascended Mystery.

sentences.zh: 薛頤者，滑州人。

translations.literal: Xue Yi was a man of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Yi came from Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 當隋大業時為道士，善天步律歷。

translations.literal: In Sui Daye times he was a Daoist priest, skilled in pacing heaven, pitch pipes, and calendars.
translations.idiomatic: During the Sui Daye era he was a Daoist priest, skilled in astronomy, pitch pipes, and calendrical science.

sentences.zh: 武德初，追直秦王府，密語曰：「德星舍秦分，王當帝天下。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he was posted on duty at the Prince of Qin's mansion and spoke secretly: "The Virtue Star lodges in Qin's division—the prince will become emperor of all under heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wude he was assigned to the Prince of Qin's household and whispered, "The Virtue Star lodges in Qin's asterism—the prince will rule the realm."

sentences.zh: 王表為太史丞，稍遷令。

translations.literal: The prince recommended him as Vice Director of the Astronomical Bureau, and he was gradually advanced to Director.
translations.idiomatic: The prince recommended him as vice director of the Astronomical Bureau, and he rose step by step to director.

sentences.zh: 貞觀時，太宗將封泰山，彗星見，賾因言：「臣商天意，陛下未可東。」

translations.literal: In Zhenguan, when Taizong was about to perform feng on Mount Tai, a comet appeared; Yi therefore said, "Your servant has consulted heaven's intent—Your Majesty should not go east."
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenguan, as Taizong prepared to perform the feng rite on Mount Tai, a comet appeared. Yi said, "I have read heaven's intent—Your Majesty should not travel east."

sentences.zh: 亦會大臣上議，帝遂罷。

translations.literal: It also happened that ministers memorialized, and the emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers also memorialized against the journey, and the emperor abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 固丐為道士，帝為築觀九嵏山，號曰：「紫府」，拜賾太中大夫，往居之。

translations.literal: He firmly begged to become a Daoist priest; the emperor built for him an abbey on Jiuxiu Mountain, styled Purple Mansion, appointed Yi Grand Master for Palace Grandee, and he went to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: He begged to return to the Daoist life. The emperor built him an abbey on Jiuxiu Mountain called "Purple Mansion," named him Grand Master for Palace Grandee, and sent him to live there.

sentences.zh: 即祠建清臺，候辰次災祥以聞，所上與太史李淳風合。

translations.literal: At the shrine he built the Clear Platform, observed the chronology of omens and disasters and reported them; what he submitted agreed with Astronomical Director Li Chunfeng.
translations.idiomatic: At the shrine he built the Clear Platform to watch celestial omens and report them; his findings matched those of Li Chunfeng at the Astronomical Bureau.

sentences.zh: 數歲卒。

translations.literal: After several years he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died a few years later.

sentences.zh: 高宗時，又有葉法善者，括州括蒼人。

translations.literal: In Gaozong's time there was also Ye Fashan, a native of Kuocang in Kuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong there was also Ye Fashan, from Kuocang in Kuozhou.

sentences.zh: 世為道士，傳陰陽、占繇、符架之術，能厭劾怪鬼。

translations.literal: For generations his family were Daoist priests; he transmitted yin-yang arts, divination by yarrow, and talisman frameworks, and could suppress and exorcise strange ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been Daoists for generations. He mastered yin-yang lore, yarrow divination, and talisman craft, and could exorcise demonic spirits.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，召詣京師，欲寵以官，不拜。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of him, summoned him to the capital, wished to honor him with office, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him to the capital and offered him office, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 留內齋場，禮賜殊縟。

translations.literal: He was kept in the inner fasting hall and received gifts and courtesies of exceptional richness.
translations.idiomatic: He remained in the inner fasting precinct and received lavish imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 時帝悉召方士，化黃金治丹，法善上言：「丹不可遽就，徒費財與日，請核真偽。」

translations.literal: At the time the emperor had summoned all fangshi to transmute gold and refine elixirs; Fashan submitted, saying, "The elixir cannot be completed hastily—it only wastes wealth and days. I ask to verify truth and falsehood."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had gathered occult masters to transmute gold and brew elixirs. Fashan memorialized, "Elixirs cannot be rushed—they only waste treasure and time. Let me test who is genuine."

sentences.zh: 帝許之，凡百餘人皆罷。

translations.literal: The emperor approved; over a hundred men were all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and more than a hundred practitioners were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 嘗在東都淩空祠為壇以祭，都人悉往觀，有數十人自奔火中，眾大驚，救而免。

translations.literal: Once at the Lingkong Shrine in the Eastern Capital he made an altar for sacrifice; all the capital went to watch, and several dozen men of themselves rushed into the fire; the crowd was greatly alarmed and they were rescued and spared.
translations.idiomatic: Once at the Lingkong Shrine in the eastern capital he set up a sacrificial altar. The whole city came to watch when dozens of people suddenly rushed into the flames. The crowd panicked, but they were pulled out unharmed.

sentences.zh: 法善笑曰：「此為魅所馮，吾以法攝之耳。」

translations.literal: Fashan laughed and said, "These were possessed by demons—I have captured them by method, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Fashan laughed and said, "Demons had possessed them—I have bound them by ritual, that is all."

sentences.zh: 問而信，病亦皆已。

translations.literal: When questioned they believed it, and their illnesses were also all cured.
translations.idiomatic: When questioned they believed him, and their ailments vanished.

sentences.zh: 其譎幻類若此。

translations.literal: His deceptions and illusions were of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His tricks and illusions were of this kind.

sentences.zh: 歷高、中二宗朝五十年，往來山中，時時召入禁內。

translations.literal: Through the reigns of the two emperors Gaozong and Zhongzong for fifty years he went back and forth in the mountains and was from time to time summoned into the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: For fifty years under Gaozong and Zhongzong he moved between mountain retreats and the inner palace, summoned whenever the court wished.

sentences.zh: 雅不喜浮屠法，常力詆毀，議者淺其好習，然發衛高，卒叵之測。

translations.literal: He naturally disliked Buddhist law and often strenuously slandered it; critics thought shallow his preferred practices, yet his cleverness was high and in the end none could fathom him.
translations.idiomatic: He detested Buddhism and often attacked it openly. Critics thought his tastes shallow, yet his wit was keen and in the end no one could fathom him.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，或言陰有助力。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, some said he had secretly assisted.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, some said Fashan had secretly aided him.

sentences.zh: 無天中，拜鴻廬卿，員外置，封越國公，舍景龍觀，追贈其父歙州刺史，寵映當世。

translations.literal: Later, under Zhongzong, he was appointed Grand Master of Ceremonies, with an extra-staff appointment; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Yue, given residence at Jinglong Abbey, and his father was posthumously honored as prefect of Shezhou—his favor shone upon the age.
translations.idiomatic: Later, under Zhongzong, he was appointed Grand Master of Ceremonies on an extra-staff basis, enfeoffed as Duke of Yue, and given quarters at Jinglong Abbey; his father was posthumously honored as prefect of Shezhou, and his favor outshone all his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 開元八年卒。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaiyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 或言生隋大業丙子，死庚子，蓋百七歲雲。

translations.literal: Some say he was born in the bingzi year of Daye in Sui and died in the gengzi year—about one hundred and seven years, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Some said he was born in the bingzi year of Daye under the Sui and died in a gengzi year—about one hundred and seven years old, it was said.

sentences.zh: 玄宗下詔褒悼，贈越州都督。

translations.literal: Xuanzong issued an edict praising and mourning him, and posthumously conferred on him the title of area commander of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong issued an edict praising and mourning him and posthumously made him area commander of Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 明崇儼，洛州偃師人，梁國子祭酒山賓五世孫。

translations.literal: Ming Chongyan was a man of Yanshi in Luozhou, fifth-generation descendant of Shanbin, Chancellor of the National University under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Chongyan was from Yanshi in Luozhou, a fifth-generation descendant of Shanbin, chancellor of the National University under Liang.

sentences.zh: 少隨父恪令安喜，吏有能召鬼神者，盡傳其術。

translations.literal: In youth he followed his father Ke to serve as magistrate of Anxi; there was an official who could summon ghosts and spirits, and he fully transmitted his arts to him.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he accompanied his father Ke to Anxi, where his father served as magistrate; an official there who could summon ghosts and spirits taught him all his techniques.

sentences.zh: 乾封初，應嶽牧舉，調黃安丞，以奇技自名。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfeng he responded to the recommendation of the mountain governor, was assigned as assistant magistrate of Huang'an, and made a name for himself through wondrous skills.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Qianfeng era he entered service through a recommendation from a mountain governor and was posted as assistant magistrate of Huang'an, where he made a name for himself with his uncanny arts.

sentences.zh: 高宗召見，甚悅，擢冀王府文學。

translations.literal: Gaozong summoned and received him, was greatly pleased, and promoted him to literary attendant in the Princely Establishment of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong summoned him, was greatly pleased, and appointed him literary attendant in the Princely Establishment of Ji.

sentences.zh: 試為窟室，使宮人奏樂其中，召崇儼問：「何祥邪？

translations.literal: He tested him by having a chamber hollowed out, had palace women play music inside, and summoned Chongyan to ask: "What omen is this?
translations.idiomatic: To test him, he had a chamber hollowed out and palace women play music inside, then summoned Chongyan and asked, "What omen is this?

sentences.zh: 為我止之。」

translations.literal: Stop it for me."
translations.idiomatic: Stop it for me."

sentences.zh: 崇儼書桃木為二符，剚室上，樂即止，曰：「向見怪龍，怖而止。」

translations.literal: Chongyan wrote two talismans on peachwood, stuck them on the chamber, and the music stopped at once. He said: "Just now I saw a strange dragon and, in fright, made it stop."
translations.idiomatic: Chongyan wrote two talismans on peachwood, affixed them to the chamber, and the music stopped at once. He said, "I just saw a strange dragon and, frightened, made it stop."

sentences.zh: 盛夏，帝思雪，崇儼坐頃取以進，自雲往陰山取之。

translations.literal: In midsummer the emperor longed for snow; Chongyan, after sitting a moment, brought some and presented it, saying himself that he had gone to the Yin Mountains to fetch it.
translations.idiomatic: In midsummer the emperor craved snow; after sitting briefly Chongyan brought some and presented it, claiming he had fetched it from the Yin Mountains.

sentences.zh: 四月，帝憶瓜，崇儼索百錢，須臾以瓜獻，曰：「得之緱氏老人圃中。」

translations.literal: In the fourth month the emperor remembered melons; Chongyan asked for a hundred cash, and in a moment presented a melon, saying: "I obtained it in the garden of an old man of Gou."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the emperor wanted melons; Chongyan asked for a hundred cash and, in a moment, presented one, saying, "I got this from an old man's garden at Gou."

sentences.zh: 帝召老人問故，曰：「埋一瓜失之，土中得百錢。」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the old man and asked the reason; he said: "I buried a melon and lost it, but found a hundred cash in the soil."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned the old man and asked what had happened; he said, "I buried a melon and lost it, but found a hundred cash in the soil."

sentences.zh: 累遷正諫大夫。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Regular Grand Master of Remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Regular Grand Master of Remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 帝令入閣供奉，每謁見，陳時政，多托鬼神為言。

translations.literal: The emperor had him enter the inner hall in attendance; whenever he was received in audience he set forth affairs of the time, often couching his words through ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had him attend within the inner hall, and whenever he was received in audience he spoke on current affairs, often framing his remarks through ghosts and spirits.

sentences.zh: 至為武後作厭勝事，又言章懷太子不德。

translations.literal: He even performed counter-magic rites for Empress Wu and also said that Crown Prince Zhanghuai was without virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He even performed counter-magic rites for Empress Wu and declared that Crown Prince Zhanghuai lacked virtue.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳四年，為盜所刺於東都，好事者為言：「崇儼役鬼勞苦，為鬼所殺。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yifeng he was stabbed by robbers in the eastern capital; those fond of marvels said: "Chongyan overworked ghosts in their service and was killed by ghosts."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yifeng he was stabbed by robbers in the eastern capital; lovers of marvels said, "Chongyan overworked the ghosts he commanded, and the ghosts killed him."

sentences.zh: 而太后疑太子使客殺之，故贈侍中，謚曰莊，擢子珪為秘書郎。

translations.literal: But the Empress Dowager suspected the crown prince had sent retainers to kill him; therefore he was posthumously given the title of Palace Attendant, with the posthumous name Zhuang, and his son Gui was promoted to secretary in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: But the Empress Dowager suspected the crown prince had sent agents to kill him; he was therefore posthumously made Palace Attendant with the posthumous name Zhuang, and his son Gui was promoted to secretary in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 命御史中丞崔謐等雜治，誣服者甚眾。

translations.literal: She ordered the censor-in-chief Cui Mi and others to conduct a joint investigation, and very many were forced by false charges to confess.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered the censor-in-chief Cui Mi and others to conduct a joint investigation, and a great many people were coerced into false confessions.

sentences.zh: 及太子廢，死狀乃明。

translations.literal: When the crown prince was deposed, the circumstances of the death became clear.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the crown prince was deposed did the true circumstances of the killing become clear.

sentences.zh: 尚獻甫，衛州汲人，善占候。

translations.literal: Shang Xianfu was a man of Ji in Weizhou and skilled in divination by celestial signs.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Xianfu was from Ji in Weizhou and skilled in reading celestial omens.

sentences.zh: 武後召見，由道士擢太史令，辭曰：「臣梗野，不可以事官長。」

translations.literal: Empress Wu summoned and received him and, from his status as a Daoist priest, promoted him to Director of the Astronomy Bureau; he declined, saying: "Your servant is blunt and uncouth and cannot serve official superiors."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu summoned him and, though he was only a Daoist priest, appointed him Director of the Astronomy Bureau; he declined, saying, "I am blunt and uncouth and cannot serve under official superiors."

sentences.zh: 後改太史局為渾儀監，以獻甫為令，不隸秘書省。

translations.literal: Thereupon she changed the Astronomy Bureau into the Directorate of the Armillary Sphere and made Xianfu its director, no longer subordinate to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: She then renamed the Astronomy Bureau the Directorate of the Armillary Sphere, made Xianfu its director, and removed it from the jurisdiction of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 數問災異，又於上陽宮集術家撰《方域》等篇。

translations.literal: She repeatedly questioned him about disasters and anomalies, and also gathered masters of the arts at Shangyang Palace to compile such works as "Regional Domains."
translations.idiomatic: She repeatedly questioned him about disasters and portents and also gathered experts at Shangyang Palace to compile works such as "Regional Domains."

sentences.zh: 長安二年，熒惑犯五諸侯，獻甫自陳：「五諸侯，太史位；

translations.literal: In the second year of Chang'an, Mars encroached upon the Five Feudal Lords; Xianfu declared of himself: "The Five Feudal Lords are the station of the Director of Astronomy;
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chang'an, Mars encroached on the Five Feudal Lords; Xianfu declared, "The Five Feudal Lords mark the station of the Director of Astronomy;

sentences.zh: 臣命納音，金也；

translations.literal: your servant's fate-element in the received tones is metal;
translations.idiomatic: my fate-element in the received tones is metal;

sentences.zh: 火，金之仇，臣且死。」

translations.literal: fire is metal's enemy—your servant is about to die."
translations.idiomatic: fire is the enemy of metal—I am about to die."

sentences.zh: 後曰：「朕為卿厭之。」

translations.literal: The Empress said: "I shall perform counter-magic for you."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress said, "I will perform counter-magic for you."

sentences.zh: 迂水衡都尉，謂曰：「水生金，卿無憂。」

translations.literal: She transferred him to be Commandant of the Directorate of Waterways and said: "Water generates metal—you need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: She transferred him to the post of Commandant of the Directorate of Waterways and said, "Water generates metal—you need not worry."

sentences.zh: 至秋卒，後嗟異，復以渾儀監為太史局云。

translations.literal: By autumn he died; the Empress sighed in wonder and restored the Directorate of the Armillary Sphere to the Astronomy Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He died that autumn; the Empress marveled and restored the Directorate of the Armillary Sphere to the Astronomy Bureau.

sentences.zh: 嚴善思名譔，同州朝邑人，以字行。

translations.literal: Yan Shansi, personal name Zan, was a man of Chaoyi in Tongzhou and was known by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shansi, personal name Zan, was from Chaoyi in Tongzhou and was known by his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 父延，與河東裴玄證、隴西李貞蔡靜皆通儒術，該曉圖識。

translations.literal: His father Yan, together with Pei Xuanzheng of Hedong and Li Zhen and Cai Jing of Longxi, were all versed in Confucian learning and thoroughly understood charts and prognostications.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan, together with Pei Xuanzheng of Hedong and Li Zhen and Cai Jing of Longxi, were all versed in Confucian learning and thoroughly understood charts and prognostications.

sentences.zh: 善思傳延業，褚遂良、上官儀等奇其能。

translations.literal: Shansi inherited Yan's profession; Chu Suiliang, Shangguan Yi, and others marveled at his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Shansi inherited his father's profession, and Chu Suiliang, Shangguan Yi, and others marveled at his ability.

sentences.zh: 高宗封泰山，舉銷聲幽藪科及第，調襄陽尉。

translations.literal: When Gaozong performed the feng sacrifice at Mount Tai, Shansi passed the examination category for reclusive talent in hidden places and was assigned as magistrate of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong performed the feng sacrifice at Mount Tai, Shansi passed the examination for reclusive talent and was posted as magistrate of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 居親喪，廬墓，因隱居十年。

translations.literal: While in mourning for a parent he built a hut at the tomb and thereafter lived in seclusion for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning a parent he built a hut at the tomb and then lived in seclusion for ten years.

sentences.zh: 武後時擢監察御史，兼右拾遺內供奉，數言天下事。

translations.literal: Under Empress Wu he was promoted to investigating censor and concurrently served as right remonstrance official in inner attendance, repeatedly speaking on affairs of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu he was promoted to investigating censor and also served as right remonstrance official in inner attendance, repeatedly speaking on affairs of the realm.

sentences.zh: 方酷吏構大獄，以善思為詳審使，平活八百餘人，原千餘姓。

translations.literal: Just as harsh officials were fabricating major cases, Shansi was made commissioner for detailed review and restored more than eight hundred persons to life and pardoned more than a thousand families.
translations.idiomatic: While harsh officials were fabricating major prosecutions, Shansi was appointed commissioner for detailed review; he saved more than eight hundred lives and pardoned more than a thousand families.

sentences.zh: 長壽中，按囚司刑寺，罷疑不實者百人。

translations.literal: During the Changshou era he reviewed prisoners at the Court of Judicial Review and dismissed a hundred whose guilt was doubtful or unfounded.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changshou era he reviewed prisoners at the Court of Judicial Review and released a hundred whose cases were doubtful or unfounded.

sentences.zh: 來俊臣等疾之，誣以罪，適交趾，五歲得還。

translations.literal: Lai Junchen and others hated him, falsely charged him with crimes, and sent him to Jiaozhi; after five years he was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Junchen and others hated him, falsely charged him with crimes, and exiled him to Jiaozhi; after five years he was allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 是時李淳風死，候家皆不效，乃詔善思以著作佐郎兼太史令。

translations.literal: At that time Li Chunfeng had died and none among the diviners proved effective, so an edict appointed Shansi Associate Editorial Director concurrently serving as Director of the Astronomy Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Chunfeng had died and none of the diviners proved effective, so the court appointed Shansi Associate Editorial Director and concurrent Director of the Astronomy Bureau.

sentences.zh: 聖歷二年，熒惑入輿鬼，後問其占，對曰：「大臣當之。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenglie, Mars entered the Celestial Coach and Ghosts; the Empress asked the meaning of the omen, and he replied: "A great minister will suffer it."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shenglie, Mars entered the Celestial Coach and Ghosts; when the Empress asked what the omen meant, he replied, "A great minister will bear it."

sentences.zh: 是年王及善卒。

translations.literal: That year Wang Jishan died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wang Jishan died.

sentences.zh: 長安中，熒惑入月，鎮犯天關，善思曰：「法當亂臣伏罪，而有下謀上之象。」

translations.literal: During the Chang'an era, Mars entered the moon and its garrison encroached upon Heavenly Pass; Shansi said: "By rule rebellious ministers should be punished, yet there is the sign of subordinates plotting against superiors."
translations.idiomatic: During the Chang'an era, Mars entered the moon and its garrison encroached on Heavenly Pass; Shansi said, "By rule rebellious ministers should be punished, yet this shows subordinates plotting against their superiors."

sentences.zh: 歲餘，張柬之等起兵誅二張。

translations.literal: More than a year later Zhang Jianzhi and others raised troops and executed the Two Zhangs.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later Zhang Jianzhi and others raised troops and executed the Two Zhangs.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 後崩，將合葬乾陵，善思建言：「尊者先葬，卑者不得入。
