translations.literal: After the Empress died, when they were about to bury her together with Gaozong at Qianling, Shansi submitted a memorial saying: "The honored one was buried first; the lesser may not enter.
translations.idiomatic: After the Empress died, when the court planned to bury her together with Gaozong at Qianling, Shansi submitted a memorial saying, "The honored one was buried first; the lesser may not enter.

sentences.zh: 今啟乾陵，是以卑動尊，術家所忌。

translations.literal: Now to open Qianling is to move the lesser against the honored—what masters of the arts dread.
translations.idiomatic: To open Qianling now would move the lesser against the honored—something masters of the arts dread.

sentences.zh: 且玄關石門，冶金錮隙，非攻鑿不能開，神道幽靜，多所驚黷。

translations.literal: Moreover, the stone gates of the hidden portal are sealed with smelted metal in the crevices; they cannot be opened without force and chiseling—the spirit path is secluded and quiet, and would be greatly disturbed and profaned.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the stone gates of the hidden portal are sealed with molten metal in the joints; they cannot be opened without force and chiseling—the spirit path is secluded and quiet and would be greatly disturbed and profaned.

sentences.zh: 若別攻隧以入其中，即往昔葬時神位前定，更且有害。

translations.literal: If one separately bores a tunnel to enter within, then the spirit's place fixed at the time of the earlier burial would be further harmed.
translations.idiomatic: If a separate tunnel were dug to enter the tomb, the spirit's place fixed at the earlier burial would be further harmed.

sentences.zh: 曩營乾陵，國有大難，易姓建國二十餘年，今又營之，難且復生。

translations.literal: When Qianling was first built the state suffered great calamity and changed surnames to establish a new dynasty for more than twenty years; now to build it again, calamity will arise once more.
translations.idiomatic: When Qianling was first built the state suffered great calamity and the dynasty changed surnames for more than twenty years; to work on it again would bring calamity once more.

sentences.zh: 合葬非古也，況事有不安，豈足循據？

translations.literal: Joint burial is not the ancient way, and moreover when the matter is unsettled, how can it serve as a precedent to follow?
translations.idiomatic: Joint burial is not the ancient way, and when the matter itself is unsettled, how can it serve as a precedent?

sentences.zh: 漢世皇后別起陵墓，魏、晉始合葬。

translations.literal: In Han times empresses had separate tombs built; only from Wei and Jin did joint burial begin.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times empresses had separate tombs built; joint burial began only under Wei and Jin.

sentences.zh: 漢積祀四百，魏、晉祚率不長，亦其驗也。

translations.literal: Han accumulated sacrifices for four hundred years, while Wei and Jin in general did not long endure—these too are proofs.
translations.idiomatic: Han endured for four hundred years, while Wei and Jin generally did not last long—this too is proof.

sentences.zh: 今若更擇吉地，附近乾陵，取從葬之義。

translations.literal: If now one selects another auspicious site near Qianling, taking the principle of attendant burial—
translations.idiomatic: If another auspicious site were chosen near Qianling, following the principle of attendant burial—

sentences.zh: 使神有知，無所不通；

translations.literal: if the spirit has awareness, nothing would be blocked;
translations.idiomatic: if the spirit has awareness, nothing would be blocked;

sentences.zh: 若其無知，合亦何益？

translations.literal: if it has no awareness, what benefit would joint burial bring?
translations.idiomatic: if it has no awareness, what good would joint burial do?

sentences.zh: 山川精氣，上為列星。

translations.literal: The vital essence of mountains and rivers rises above to become the arrayed stars.
translations.idiomatic: The vital essence of mountains and rivers rises to become the arrayed stars.

sentences.zh: 葬得其所，則神安而後嗣昌；

translations.literal: When burial obtains its proper place, the spirit is at peace and later generations flourish;
translations.idiomatic: When burial finds its proper place, the spirit is at peace and later generations flourish;

sentences.zh: 失其宜，則神危而後嗣損。

translations.literal: when it misses what is fitting, the spirit is endangered and later generations are harmed.
translations.idiomatic: when it misses what is fitting, the spirit is endangered and later generations suffer.

sentences.zh: 願割私愛，使社稷長久。」

translations.literal: I beg that private affection be set aside so that the altars of state may long endure."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that private affection be set aside so that the altars of state may long endure."

sentences.zh: 中宗不納。

translations.literal: Zhongzong did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzong did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 神龍中，武後喪公除，太常請大習樂，供郊廟，詔未許。

translations.literal: During the Shenlong era, when the mourning for Empress Wu had reached public termination, the Minister of Ceremonies requested extensive rehearsal of music to supply the suburban and ancestral temples; an edict did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shenlong era, when the mourning for Empress Wu had reached public termination, the Minister of Ceremonies requested extensive rehearsal of music for the suburban and ancestral temples, but the edict did not grant it.

sentences.zh: 善思奏曰：「樂者氣化，所以感天地、調五行。

translations.literal: Shansi submitted a memorial saying: "Music is the transformation of qi, by which one moves Heaven and Earth and harmonizes the Five Phases.
translations.idiomatic: Shansi submitted a memorial saying, "Music is the transformation of qi, by which one moves Heaven and Earth and harmonizes the Five Phases.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏喪禮，以日易月，蓋三年不為禮，禮必壞，三年不為樂，樂必崩。

translations.literal: In Han and Wei mourning rites, days were substituted for months, for if for three years one does not perform rites, rites must collapse; if for three years one does not perform music, music must crumble.
translations.idiomatic: In Han and Wei mourning rites, days were substituted for months, for if rites are not performed for three years, rites must collapse; if music is not performed for three years, music must crumble.

sentences.zh: 禮，陰也；

translations.literal: Rites are yin;
translations.idiomatic: Rites are yin;

sentences.zh: 樂，陽也。

translations.literal: music is yang.
translations.idiomatic: music is yang.

sentences.zh: 樂崩陽伏，禮廢陰愆，故變以適時，孝道之大。

translations.literal: When music crumbles, yang is hidden; when rites are abandoned, yin is in fault—therefore to change in accord with the times is the greatness of filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When music crumbles, yang is hidden; when rites are abandoned, yin is in fault—therefore to adapt to the times is the highest form of filial piety.

sentences.zh: 安人神，公也；

translations.literal: To settle the spirits of the people is public duty;
translations.idiomatic: To settle the spirits of the people is a public duty;

sentences.zh: 茹哀戚，私也。

translations.literal: to nourish grief and sorrow is private feeling.
translations.idiomatic: to nourish grief and sorrow is a private feeling.

sentences.zh: 王者不以私害公，請如太常奏。」

translations.literal: A king does not let private feeling harm public duty—I request that it be as the Minister of Ceremonies proposed."
translations.idiomatic: A ruler must not let private feeling harm public duty—I request that the Minister of Ceremonies' proposal be approved."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 表皇后擅政，為社稷憂，求汝州刺史。

translations.literal: He memorialized that the empress was monopolizing government, expressed concern for the altars of state, and requested the post of prefect of Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized that the empress was monopolizing government, expressed concern for the altars of state, and requested appointment as prefect of Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗語姚崇曰：「韋氏禍且塗地，相王所居有華蓋紫氣，必位九五，公善護之。」

translations.literal: He once said to Yao Chong: "The Wei clan's calamity will soon cover the earth; where the Prince of Xiang dwells there is the purple vapor of the Canopy—he will surely attain the throne; you must protect him well."
translations.idiomatic: He once told Yao Chong, "The Wei clan's calamity will soon cover the land; purple vapor of the Canopy hangs over the Prince of Xiang's residence—he will surely attain the throne. Protect him well."

sentences.zh: 及睿宗立，崇以語聞，召拜右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, Chong reported these words and Shansi was summoned and appointed Right Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong took the throne, Chong reported these words, and Shansi was summoned and appointed Right Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，譙王重福徙均州，過汝，善思為刺史。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Prince of Qiao Chongfu was transferred to Junzhou he passed through Ru, where Shansi was prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Prince of Qiao Chongfu was transferred to Junzhou he passed through Ruzhou, where Shansi was prefect.

sentences.zh: 及謀反，偽除禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When he plotted rebellion he falsely appointed Shansi Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongfu plotted rebellion he falsely appointed Shansi Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 重福敗，坐關通論死，吏部尚書宋璟、戶部郎中李邕薄其罪，給事中韓思復固請，乃流靜州。

translations.literal: When Chongfu was defeated, Shansi was judged guilty of collusion and sentenced to death; Minister of Personnel Song Jing and bureau director Li Yong considered his offense slight, and Supervising Secretary Han Sifu firmly pleaded on his behalf, whereupon he was banished to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongfu was defeated, Shansi was convicted of collusion and sentenced to death; Minister of Personnel Song Jing and bureau director Li Yong considered his offense slight, and Supervising Secretary Han Sifu firmly pleaded for him, whereupon he was banished to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 始，善思為御史，中書舍人劉允濟為酷吏所陷，且死，善思力訟其冤，得免。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Shansi was a censor, Secretariat Drafter Liu Yunji was trapped by a harsh official and was about to die; Shansi strenuously argued his innocence and secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shansi was a censor, Secretariat Drafter Liu Yunji was framed by a harsh official and faced death; Shansi vigorously argued his innocence and secured his release.

sentences.zh: 戶部尚書王本立見之，曰：「祁奚之救叔向，嚴公有之。」

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue Wang Benli witnessed this and said: "In Yan there is one who has Qi Xi's rescue of Shu Xiang."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Wang Benli witnessed this and said, "Yan has its own Qi Xi rescuing Shu Xiang."

sentences.zh: 後見允濟，語未嘗及之。

translations.literal: Later when he met Yunji, in conversation he never mentioned it.
translations.idiomatic: Later when he met Yunji, he never mentioned it in conversation.

sentences.zh: 思復之解善思也，亦不自德，時稱長者之報。

translations.literal: When Sifu secured Shansi's release, he too did not claim merit for himself; the age praised it as the reward due a man of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When Sifu secured Shansi's release, he too did not claim credit; contemporaries praised it as the reward due a man of virtue.

sentences.zh: 後遇赦還。

translations.literal: Later he returned upon encountering an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: He later returned under an amnesty.

sentences.zh: 開元十六年卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 子向，乾元中為鳳翔尹，三世皆年八十五雲。

translations.literal: His son Xiang, in the Qianyuan era served as prefect of Fengxiang; three generations all reached eighty-five years, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiang served as prefect of Fengxiang in the Qianyuan era; it was said that three generations of the family all lived to eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 杜生者，許州人。

translations.literal: Master Du was a man of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Master Du was from Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 善《易》占。

translations.literal: He was skilled in divination by the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in divination with the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 有亡奴者問所從追，戒曰：「自此行，逢使者，懇丐其鞭。

translations.literal: Someone whose slave had fled asked which direction to pursue; he warned him, saying: "From here go forth; when you meet a messenger, earnestly beg his whip.
translations.idiomatic: A man whose slave had run away asked which direction to pursue; Du warned him, saying, "Go on from here; when you meet a messenger, earnestly beg his whip.

sentences.zh: 若不可，則以情告。」

translations.literal: If that is not possible, then tell him your situation."
translations.idiomatic: If that fails, tell him your situation."

sentences.zh: 其人果值使者於道，如生語，使者異之，曰：「去鞭，吾無以進馬，可折道傍葼代之。」

translations.literal: The man indeed met a messenger on the road; as Master Du had said, he spoke, and the messenger, finding it strange, said: "Leave the whip—I have no way to drive my horse; you may break roadside rushes to replace it."
translations.idiomatic: The man did meet a messenger on the road; following Du's instructions, he spoke, and the messenger, surprised, said, "Keep the whip—I have no way to drive my horse; break roadside rushes to replace it."

sentences.zh: 乃往折葼，見亡奴伏其下，獲之。

translations.literal: He then went to break rushes and saw the runaway slave crouching beneath them and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: He went to break rushes and found the runaway slave hiding beneath them and captured him.

sentences.zh: 它日又有亡奴者，生戒持錢五百伺於道，見進鷂使者，可市其一，必得奴。

translations.literal: Another day another man whose slave had fled came; Master Du warned him to hold five hundred cash and wait on the road; when he saw a messenger bringing hawks, he could buy one of them and would surely recover the slave.
translations.idiomatic: Another day a man whose slave had run away came; Du told him to take five hundred cash and wait on the road; when he saw a messenger bringing hawks, he should buy one and would surely recover the slave.

sentences.zh: 俄而使至，其人以情告，使者以一與之，忽飛集灌莽上，往取之而得亡奴。

translations.literal: Before long the messenger arrived; the man told his situation, and the messenger gave him one; it suddenly flew and alighted on a thicket, and when he went to take it he found the runaway slave.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the messenger arrived; the man explained his situation, and the messenger gave him one hawk; it suddenly flew and alighted on a thicket, and when he went to retrieve it he found the runaway slave.

sentences.zh: 眾以為神。

translations.literal: The multitude considered him divine.
translations.idiomatic: People considered him miraculous.

sentences.zh: 時有浮屠泓者，黃州人。

translations.literal: At the time there was the Buddhist monk Hong, a man of Huangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was a Buddhist monk named Hong, from Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 與天官侍郎張敬之善。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Vice Minister of the Bureau of Astronomy Zhang Jingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He was on good terms with Vice Minister of the Bureau of Astronomy Zhang Jingzhi.

sentences.zh: 敬之以武後在位，常指所服示子冠宗曰：「莽朝服耳。」

translations.literal: Because Empress Wu was on the throne, Jingzhi often pointed to what he wore and showed his son Guanzong, saying: "This is merely the court dress of the Wang Mang dynasty."
translations.idiomatic: With Empress Wu on the throne, Jingzhi often pointed to his own robes and showed his son Guanzong, saying, "This is merely the court dress of Wang Mang's dynasty."

sentences.zh: 俄冠宗以父應入三品，詣有司言狀。

translations.literal: Before long Guanzong, on the basis of his father's entitlement, sought entry into the third rank and went to the relevant office to state the case.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Guanzong, claiming entitlement through his father's rank, sought entry into the third rank and went to the relevant office to state his case.

sentences.zh: 泓忽曰：「君無煩求三品也。」

translations.literal: Hong suddenly said: "Sir, need not trouble yourself to seek the third rank."
translations.idiomatic: Hong suddenly said, "Sir, do not trouble yourself to seek the third rank."

sentences.zh: 敬之大驚，已而知出冠宗意。

translations.literal: Jingzhi was greatly startled; afterward he learned that the remark had come from Guanzong's intention.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhi was greatly startled; afterward he learned that Hong had spoken from Guanzong's purpose.

sentences.zh: 敬之弟訥之疾殆，泓曰：「公弟當位三品，不足憂也。」

translations.literal: Jingzhi's younger brother Nezhi was critically ill. Hong said: "Your younger brother will attain the third rank; there is no need to worry."
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhi's younger brother Nezhi lay near death, Hong said, "Your brother will reach the third rank—there is no cause for alarm."

sentences.zh: 已而愈。

translations.literal: Before long he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he recovered.

sentences.zh: 嘗為燕國公張說市宅，戒曰：「無穿東北，王隅也！」

translations.literal: Once he selected a residence for Duke of Yan Zhang Yue, warning: "Do not breach the northeast—it is the king's corner!"
translations.idiomatic: He once selected a residence for Duke of Yan Zhang Yue and warned, "Do not break ground in the northeast—that corner belongs to the king!"

sentences.zh: 它日見說曰：「宅氣索然，云何？」

translations.literal: Another day he saw Yue and said: "The dwelling's vital energy is utterly depleted—what is the cause?"
translations.idiomatic: Another day he visited Yue and asked, "The house's vital energy has drained away entirely—what happened?"

sentences.zh: 與說共視，土隅有三坎丈餘，泓驚曰：「公富貴一世而已，諸子將不終。」

translations.literal: He and Yue looked together; in the earthen corner were three pits over a zhang deep. Hong cried in alarm: "My lord's wealth and honor will last but one lifetime; your sons will not come to good ends."
translations.idiomatic: Together they inspected the site and found three pits more than a zhang deep in the northeast corner. Hong cried out in alarm, "My lord's wealth and honor will endure for one lifetime only; your sons will not die well."

sentences.zh: 說懼，將平之，泓曰：「客土無氣，與地脈不連，譬身瘡痏補它肉，無益也。」

translations.literal: Yue was afraid and was about to fill them in. Hong said: "Fill soil has no vital energy and is not connected to the earth's pulse—it is like patching a body's sore with another's flesh; it is of no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Yue, frightened, was about to level the pits. Hong said, "Imported fill carries no vital energy and does not join the earth's pulse—it is like grafting foreign flesh onto a body's sore; it will do no good."

sentences.zh: 說子皆汙賊死斥云。

translations.literal: Yue's sons all died as disgraced rebels and outcasts, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Yue's sons all died as disgraced rebels and were cast out, so it is recorded.

sentences.zh: 張果者，晦鄉里世系以自神，隱中條山，往來汾、晉間，世傳數百歲人。

translations.literal: Zhang Guo obscured his native place and lineage to make himself mysterious; he hid on Mount Zhongtiao, traveling between Fen and Jin, and was transmitted in the world as a man of several hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guo concealed his hometown and lineage to cultivate an air of mystery. He lived in seclusion on Mount Zhongtiao, passing between Fen and Jin, and the world transmitted tales of him as a man of several hundred years.

sentences.zh: 武後時，遣使召之，即死，後人復見居恒州山中。

translations.literal: In Empress Wu's time, envoys were sent to summon him; he immediately died, yet later people again saw him dwelling in the mountains of Hengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Wu's reign, envoys were dispatched to summon him; he died on the spot, yet afterward people saw him again living in the mountains of Hengzhou.

sentences.zh: 開元二十一年，刺史韋濟以聞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Kaiyuan, the prefect Wei Ji reported this.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year of Kaiyuan, Prefect Wei Ji reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 玄宗令通事舍人裴晤往迎，見晤輒氣絕仆，久乃蘇。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong ordered the Diplomatic Reception Attendant Pei Wo to go and escort him. When he saw Wo he would instantly stop breathing and fall over; only after a long time would he revive.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong sent Diplomatic Reception Attendant Pei Wo to welcome him. At the sight of Wo, Guo would instantly stop breathing and collapse; only after a long while would he revive.

sentences.zh: 晤不敢逼，馳白狀。

translations.literal: Wo did not dare press him and galloped back to report the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Wo did not dare press him further and galloped back to report what had happened.

sentences.zh: 帝更遣中書舍人徐嶠賫璽書邀禮，乃至東都，舍集賢院，肩輿入宮。

translations.literal: The Emperor again sent Secretariat Drafter Xu Qiao bearing imperial edicts to invite him with ceremony; only then did he come to the Eastern Capital, lodging at the Hall of Worthies, and enter the palace in a shoulder-borne carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then sent Secretariat Drafter Xu Qiao with sealed imperial invitations. Only then did Guo come to the Eastern Capital, lodge at the Hall of Worthies, and enter the palace in a sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 帝親問治道神仙事，語秘不傳。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally questioned him on governance and matters of immortals; the words were secret and were not transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor questioned him personally on governance and the way of immortals; what was said remained secret and was never recorded.

sentences.zh: 果善息氣，能累日不食，數禦美酒。

translations.literal: Guo was skilled at breath-holding and could go many days without eating, yet often enjoyed fine wine.
translations.idiomatic: Guo could hold his breath and abstain from food for days on end, yet he often drank fine wine at court.

sentences.zh: 嘗云：「我生堯丙子歲，位侍中。」

translations.literal: He once said: "I was born in the bingzi year of Yao's reign and held the rank of Palace Attendant."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "I was born in the bingzi year of Yao's reign and served as Palace Attendant."

sentences.zh: 其貌實年六七十。

translations.literal: In appearance he was in fact sixty or seventy years old.
translations.idiomatic: In appearance he looked to be sixty or seventy.

sentences.zh: 時有邢和璞者，善知人夭壽。

translations.literal: At the time there was Xing Hebao, who was skilled at knowing a person's early death or long life.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was Xing Hebao, skilled at discerning whether a man would die young or live long.

sentences.zh: 師夜光者，善視鬼。

translations.literal: Shi Yeguang was skilled at seeing ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yeguang could see ghosts.

sentences.zh: 帝令和璞推果生死，懵然莫知其端。

translations.literal: The Emperor had Hebao calculate Guo's life and death, but he was baffled and could not know where it lay.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had Hebao calculate Guo's span of life, but he was utterly baffled and could find no answer.

sentences.zh: 帝召果密坐，使夜光視之，不見果所住。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Guo to sit close in secret and had Yeguang look at him, but he could not see where Guo was seated.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had Guo sit close beside him in secret and ordered Yeguang to look—but Yeguang could not see where Guo sat.

sentences.zh: 帝謂高力士曰：「吾聞飲堇無苦者，奇士也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to Gao Lishi: "I have heard that one who can drink hellebore without bitterness is a rare man."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said to Gao Lishi, "They say a man who can drink hellebore and taste no bitterness is no ordinary soul."

sentences.zh: 時天寒，因取以飲果，三進，頹然曰：「非佳酒也。」

translations.literal: It was cold weather, so he had it brought for Guo to drink. After three rounds Guo slumped and said: "This is not fine wine."
translations.idiomatic: The weather was bitterly cold, so the Emperor had hellebore brought for Guo to drink. After three cups Guo slumped over and said, "This is no fine wine."

sentences.zh: 乃寢。

translations.literal: Then he slept.
translations.idiomatic: Then he fell asleep.

sentences.zh: 頃視齒燋縮，顧左右取鐵如意擊墮之，藏帶中，更出藥傅其斷，良久，齒已生，粲然駢絜。

translations.literal: Presently they saw his teeth charred and shrunken; turning to those at his side he took an iron ruyi scepter, knocked them out and dropped them, hid them in his belt, then brought out medicine and applied it to the broken ends. Before long new teeth had grown, bright and neatly aligned.
translations.idiomatic: A moment later his teeth appeared charred and shriveled. He turned to his attendants, took an iron ruyi scepter, knocked the teeth out and dropped them into his belt, then produced a salve and smeared it on the broken stumps. Before long fresh teeth had grown in, white and even.

sentences.zh: 帝益神之。

translations.literal: The Emperor all the more regarded him as supernatural.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor regarded him as all the more miraculous.

sentences.zh: 欲以玉真公主降果，未言也。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to marry Princess Yuzhen to Guo, but had not yet spoken of it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor intended to give Princess Yuzhen in marriage to Guo, though he had not yet said so.

sentences.zh: 果忽謂秘書少監王迥質、太常少卿蕭華曰：「諺謂娶婦得公主，平地生公府，可畏也。」

translations.literal: Guo suddenly said to Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Huizhi and Vice Minister of Rites Xiao Hua: "A proverb says that marrying and getting a princess is like making a grand official's mansion spring up on level ground—it is dreadful."
translations.idiomatic: Guo suddenly said to Vice Director of the Secretariat Wang Huizhi and Vice Minister of Rites Xiao Hua, "There is a saying: 'Marry a princess, and a grand official's mansion springs up on level ground'—how dreadful that is."

sentences.zh: 二人怪語不倫。

translations.literal: The two men found the words strange and incongruous.
translations.idiomatic: The two men thought his words bizarre and out of place.

sentences.zh: 俄有使至，傳詔曰：「玉真公主欲降先生。」

translations.literal: Before long an envoy arrived, conveying an edict: "Princess Yuzhen wishes to marry the Master."
translations.idiomatic: Before long an envoy arrived with an edict: "Princess Yuzhen wishes to marry the Master."

sentences.zh: 果笑，固不奉詔。

translations.literal: Guo laughed and steadfastly refused to accept the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Guo laughed and firmly refused the edict.

sentences.zh: 有詔圖形集賢院，懇辭還山，詔可。

translations.literal: An edict was issued to have his likeness painted at the Hall of Worthies; he earnestly declined and returned to the mountains, and the edict granted permission.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered his portrait painted at the Hall of Worthies. He earnestly begged leave to return to the mountains, and the Emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 擢銀青光祿大夫，號通玄先生，賜帛三百匹，給扶侍二人。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, styled Master of Penetrating Mystery, granted three hundred bolts of silk, and given two attendants to support him.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, given the style Master of Penetrating Mystery, awarded three hundred bolts of silk, and provided with two attendants.

sentences.zh: 至恒山蒲吾縣，未幾卒，或言屍解。

translations.literal: Reaching Puwu County in Hengshan, before long he died—or some said his corpse dissolved and he ascended.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Puwu County in Hengshan and soon died—or so some said, while others claimed he achieved corporeal liberation.

sentences.zh: 帝為立棲霞觀其所。

translations.literal: The Emperor had a Qixia Abbey built at his dwelling place.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor built the Qixia Abbey on the site of his dwelling.

sentences.zh: 夜光者，薊州人，少為浮屠。

translations.literal: Shi Yeguang was a man of Jizhou; in youth he was a Buddhist monk.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yeguang was from Jizhou and had been a Buddhist monk in his youth.

sentences.zh: 至長安，因九仙公主得召見溫泉，帝奇其辯，賜冠帶，授四門博士，賜緋衣、銀魚、金繒千數，得侍左右如幸臣。

translations.literal: Arriving at Chang'an, through Princess Jiuxian he was summoned to an audience at the hot springs. The Emperor marveled at his eloquence, bestowed cap and belt, appointed him Erudite of the Four Gates, granted crimson robes, silver fish pendants, and silks in the thousands, and allowed him to attend at the Emperor's side like a favored minister.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Chang'an, Princess Jiuxian secured him an audience at the hot springs. The Emperor was struck by his eloquence, bestowed official cap and belt, appointed him Erudite of the Four Gates, and granted crimson robes, silver fish insignia, and silks by the thousand. He attended at the Emperor's side like a favored courtier.

sentences.zh: 和璞喜黃老，作《潁陽書》，世傳之。

translations.literal: Hebao delighted in Yellow Emperor and Laozi teachings and wrote the Book of Yingyang, which was transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Hebao devoted himself to Yellow Emperor and Laozi teachings and wrote the Book of Yingyang, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，有孫甑生者，以技聞，能使石自鬥，草為人騎馳走。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era there was Sun Zaosheng, famed for his arts: he could make stones fight on their own and grass figures mounted as men gallop about.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era there was Sun Zaosheng, renowned for his tricks: he could set stones to fighting by themselves and shape grass into mounted riders that galloped about.

sentences.zh: 楊貴妃喜觀之，數召入宮中。

translations.literal: Consort Yang Guifei delighted in watching him and repeatedly summoned him into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yang Guifei loved to watch his performances and repeatedly summoned him to the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 又有羅思遠，能自隱。

translations.literal: There was also Luo Siyuan, who could render himself invisible.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Luo Siyuan, who could make himself invisible.

sentences.zh: 帝學，不肯盡其術，試自隱，常餘衣帶，及思遠共試，則驗。

translations.literal: The Emperor learned from him, but Luo would not teach the whole art to completion. When the Emperor tried to conceal himself, clothing and belt often remained visible; but when tested together with Siyuan, the effect was verified.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor studied under him, but Luo would not teach the full technique. When the Emperor tried to vanish on his own, strips of clothing and belt often remained in view; only when Luo joined the attempt did the trick succeed.

sentences.zh: 厚錫金帛，然卒不得。

translations.literal: The Emperor richly rewarded him with gold and silks, yet in the end could not obtain the full technique.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor heaped gold and silks upon him, yet never obtained the complete art.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，裹以襆，壓殺之。

translations.literal: The Emperor in anger wrapped him in a bundled cloth and crushed him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the Emperor had him wrapped in a cloth bundle and crushed to death.

sentences.zh: 數日，有中使者自蜀還，逢思遠駕而西，笑曰：「上為戲何虐也！」

translations.literal: Several days later, a palace envoy returning from Shu met Siyuan driving westward; he laughed and said: "Your Majesty's jest—how cruel!"
translations.idiomatic: Several days later a palace envoy returning from Shu encountered Siyuan driving westward. Siyuan laughed and said, "What a cruel jest Your Majesty plays!"

sentences.zh: 姜撫，宋州人。

translations.literal: Jiang Fu was a man of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Fu was from Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 自言通仙人不死術，隱居不出。

translations.literal: He claimed mastery of immortals' arts of non-death and lived in seclusion without emerging.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed to know the immortals' art of escaping death and lived in seclusion, never venturing out.

sentences.zh: 開元末，太常卿韋縚祭名山，因訪隱民，還白撫已數百歲。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyuan, Minister of Ceremonies Wei Tao sacrificed at famous mountains and, while visiting recluses, returned reporting that Fu was already several hundred years old.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Kaiyuan, Minister of Ceremonies Wei Tao, while performing sacrifices at famous mountains, visited recluses and returned reporting that Fu was already several hundred years old.

sentences.zh: 召至東都，舍集賢院。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the Eastern Capital and lodged at the Hall of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was summoned to the Eastern Capital and housed at the Hall of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 因言：「服常春藤，使白髮還鬢，則長生可致。

translations.literal: He then said: "By taking ever-spring vine, turning white hair back to dark temples, one can attain long life.
translations.idiomatic: He declared, "Take the ever-spring vine and white hair will return to dark temples—long life can be attained.

sentences.zh: 藤生太湖最良，終南往往有之，不及也。」

translations.literal: The vine grows best at Lake Tai; it is often found on Zhongnan as well, but does not compare."
translations.idiomatic: The vine grows finest at Lake Tai. It is sometimes found on Zhongnan Mountain, but never equals the Tai stock."

sentences.zh: 帝遣使者至太湖，多取以賜中朝老臣。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent envoys to Lake Tai and had much gathered to bestow on senior ministers at court.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent envoys to Lake Tai, gathered great quantities, and bestowed them on senior ministers at court.

sentences.zh: 因詔天下，使自求之。

translations.literal: Accordingly an edict went throughout the realm, ordering people to seek it for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then went out to the realm, commanding everyone to seek the vine for themselves.

sentences.zh: 宰相裴耀卿奉觴上千萬歲壽，帝悅，禦花萼棲宴群臣，出藤百奩，遍賜之。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Pei Yaojing raised a cup wishing ten thousand years of life; the Emperor was pleased, held a banquet for the assembled ministers at Hua'e Pavilion, brought out a hundred caskets of vine, and distributed them to all.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Pei Yaojing raised a cup to wish the Emperor ten thousand years of life. Delighted, the Emperor hosted the assembled ministers at Hua'e Pavilion, produced a hundred caskets of vine, and distributed them to all present.

sentences.zh: 擢撫銀青光祿大夫，號沖和先生。

translations.literal: Fu was promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and styled Master of Harmonious Equilibrium.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was promoted to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and given the style Master of Harmonious Equilibrium.

sentences.zh: 撫又言：「終南山有旱藕，餌之延年。」

translations.literal: Fu further said: "On Zhongnan Mountain there is drought-lotus root; eating it prolongs life."
translations.idiomatic: Fu added, "On Zhongnan Mountain there is drought-lotus root; eat it and you will extend your years."

sentences.zh: 狀類葛粉，帝作湯餅賜大臣。

translations.literal: Its appearance resembled kudzu powder; the Emperor made noodle soup and bestowed it on ministers.
translations.idiomatic: It resembled kudzu starch in form. The Emperor had noodle soup made from it and bestowed bowls on his ministers.

sentences.zh: 右驍衛將軍甘守誠能銘藥石，曰：「常春者，千歲藟也。

translations.literal: Right Yaoqi Guard General Gan Shoucheng, who could identify medicines by inscription, said: "Ever-spring is the thousand-year creeper.
translations.idiomatic: Right Yaoqi Guard General Gan Shoucheng, who could identify drugs and stones, said, "'Ever-spring' is the thousand-year creeper.

sentences.zh: 旱藕，杜蒙也。

translations.literal: Drought-lotus is dolomiaea.
translations.idiomatic: Drought-lotus' is dolomiaea.

sentences.zh: 方家久不用，撫易名以神之。

translations.literal: Formulas have long abandoned these; Fu changed their names to make them divine.
translations.idiomatic: Physicians abandoned these long ago. Fu merely renamed them to pass them off as miraculous.

sentences.zh: 民間以酒漬藤，飲者多暴死。」

translations.literal: Among the people, many who steeped the vine in wine and drank it died suddenly."
translations.idiomatic: Among the people, many who steeped the vine in wine and drank it died suddenly."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon the distribution stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the distribution ceased.

sentences.zh: 撫內慚悸，請求藥牢山，遂逃去。

translations.literal: Fu inwardly ashamed and fearful, requested herbs on Mount Laoshan, and then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed and afraid, Fu asked leave to gather herbs on Mount Laoshan—and fled.

sentences.zh: 桑道茂者，寒人，失其系望。

translations.literal: Sang Daomao was a man of humble birth; his lineage and ancestral status were unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Daomao was of humble birth; his lineage and clan standing were unknown.

sentences.zh: 善太一遁甲術。

translations.literal: He was skilled at Grand Unity and Dunjia divination.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in Grand Unity and Dunjia divination.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，官軍圍安慶緒於相州，勢危甚，道茂在圍中，密語人曰：「三月壬申西師潰。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyuan, government troops besieged An Qingxu at Xiangzhou; the situation was extremely perilous. Daomao was within the encirclement and privately told someone: "On the third month, renshen day, the western army will collapse."
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Qianyuan, imperial troops besieged An Qingxu at Xiangzhou in dire straits. Daomao was trapped inside the encirclement and privately told someone, "On the third month's renshen day the western army will collapse."

sentences.zh: 至期，九節度兵皆敗。

translations.literal: When the day arrived, the armies of the nine frontier commissioners were all defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When the day came, the armies of all nine frontier commissioners were routed.

sentences.zh: 後召待詔翰林。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned as a Hanlin Academician-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 建中初，上言：「國家不出三年有厄會，奉天有王氣，宜高坦堞，為王者居，使可容萬乘者。」

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong he submitted a memorial: "Within three years the state will meet calamity. Fengtian has kingly vital energy; the walls should be raised high and broad, made a dwelling for a king, able to accommodate the imperial carriage."
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianzhong he memorialized the throne: "Within three years the realm will face calamity. Fengtian bears kingly vital energy—the walls should be raised high and broad, built as a seat fit for a sovereign, spacious enough for the imperial carriage."

sentences.zh: 德宗素驗其數，詔京兆尹嚴郢發眾數千及神策兵城之。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong had long verified his calculations and ordered Metropolitan Governor Yan Ying to mobilize several thousand laborers and Shence troops to fortify it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong, who had long found Daomao's calculations accurate, ordered Metropolitan Governor Yan Ying to mobilize several thousand workers and Shence troops to fortify the city.

sentences.zh: 時盛夏趣功，人莫知其故。

translations.literal: It was the height of summer and work was rushed; no one knew the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Work was rushed through the height of summer, and no one knew why.

sentences.zh: 及朱泚反，帝蒙難奉天，賴以濟。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, the Emperor suffered hardship at Fengtian and relied on the fortification to be saved.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, the Emperor fled in distress to Fengtian and was saved by those walls.

sentences.zh: 李晟為右金吾大將軍，道茂賫一縑見晟，再拜曰：「公貴盛無比，然我命在公手，能見赦否？」

translations.literal: Li Sheng was Grand General of the Right Gold Crow Guard. Daomao brought a length of silk and visited Sheng, bowing twice and saying: "Your lordship's glory is unmatched, yet my life is in your hands—can you spare me?"
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng was Grand General of the Right Gold Crow Guard. Daomao came bearing a length of silk, bowed twice, and said, "Your glory is beyond compare, yet my life rests in your hands—will you spare me?"

sentences.zh: 晟大驚，不領其言。

translations.literal: Sheng was greatly startled and did not grasp his meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was deeply startled and could not make sense of his words.

sentences.zh: 道茂出懷中一書，自具姓名，署其左曰：「為賊逼脅。」

translations.literal: Daomao produced from his bosom a document bearing his own name, and on its left margin wrote: "Coerced by the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Daomao drew from his robe a document bearing his own name and wrote on the left margin, "Coerced by the rebels."

sentences.zh: 固請晟判，晟笑曰：「欲我何語？」

translations.literal: He pressed Sheng to endorse it. Sheng laughed and said: "What words do you wish from me?"
translations.idiomatic: He pressed Sheng to endorse it. Sheng laughed and asked, "What am I to write?"

sentences.zh: 道茂曰：「弟言準狀赦之。」

translations.literal: Daomao said: "Your younger brother asks that you pardon according to the document's terms."
translations.idiomatic: Daomao said, "Your younger brother asks that you pardon him according to this document."

sentences.zh: 晟勉從。

translations.literal: Sheng reluctantly complied.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng reluctantly agreed.

sentences.zh: 已又以縑願易晟衫，請題衿膺曰：「它日為信。」

translations.literal: Then with another length of silk he wished to exchange for Sheng's shirt and asked that the collar be inscribed: "As proof on another day."
translations.idiomatic: Then, offering another length of silk, he asked to exchange it for Sheng's shirt and requested an inscription on the collar: "As proof on another day."

sentences.zh: 再拜去。

translations.literal: He bowed twice and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed twice and left.

sentences.zh: 道茂果汙朱泚偽官。

translations.literal: Daomao did indeed become tainted as an official under Zhu Ci's false regime.
translations.idiomatic: Daomao did indeed serve as an official under Zhu Ci's puppet regime.

sentences.zh: 晟收長安，與逆徒縛旗下，將就刑，出晟衫及書以示。

translations.literal: When Sheng recovered Chang'an, Daomao was bound with rebels beneath the banner, about to be executed; he produced Sheng's shirt and the document to show them.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng retook Chang'an, Daomao was bound with the rebels beneath the execution banner. As he was about to die, he produced Sheng's shirt and the document.

sentences.zh: 晟為奏，原其死。

translations.literal: Sheng memorialized on his behalf and had his death pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng memorialized the throne on his behalf and secured a pardon.

sentences.zh: 是時藩鎮擅地無寧時，道茂曰：「年號元和，寇盜翦滅矣。」

translations.literal: At this time frontier garrisons held territory without respite; Daomao said: "Under the reign era Yuanhe, bandits and rebels will be cut down and destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: In those days the frontier garrisons seized territory without cease. Daomao said, "When the reign era is Yuanhe, bandits and rebels will be cut down and destroyed."

sentences.zh: 至憲宗乃驗。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xianzong this was verified.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianzong the prophecy was fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 道茂居有二伯甚茂，曰：「人居而木蕃者去之，木盛則土衰，土衰則人病。」

translations.literal: Two cypresses at Daomao's dwelling were very luxuriant. He said: "Where people dwell and trees flourish excessively, remove them—when wood flourishes then earth declines; when earth declines then people sicken."
translations.idiomatic: Two cypresses at Daomao's dwelling grew extravagantly lush. He said, "Where people live and trees run riot, cut them down—when wood flourishes, earth weakens; when earth weakens, people fall ill."

sentences.zh: 乃以鐵數十鈞埋其下，復曰：「後有發其地而死者。」

translations.literal: He buried several tens of jun of iron beneath them, and added: "Later one who opens this ground will die."
translations.idiomatic: He buried several tens of jun of iron beneath them and added, "Whoever later digs up this ground will die."

sentences.zh: 大和中，溫造居之，發藏鐵而造死。

translations.literal: In the Dahe reign, Wen Zao dwelt there; he unearthed the hidden iron and Zao died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dahe era Wen Zao took up residence there, unearthed the buried iron, and died.

sentences.zh: 杜佑與楊炎善。

translations.literal: Du You was on good terms with Yang Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Du You was close to Yang Yan.

sentences.zh: 盧杞疾之，佑懼，以問道茂，答曰：「君歲中補外，則福壽叵涯矣。」

translations.literal: Lu Qi resented this; You was afraid and questioned Daomao, who answered: "If you receive an outside appointment within the year, then fortune and longevity will be boundless."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qi resented their friendship. Fearful, Du You consulted Daomao, who answered, "If you receive an outside posting within the year, fortune and long life will know no limit."

sentences.zh: 俄拜饒州刺史，後終司徒。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Prefect of Raozhou; later he ended as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Prefect of Raozhou and eventually rose to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 李泌病，道茂署於紙曰：「厄三月二日就饗，國與家吉而身危。」

translations.literal: Li Mi was ill; Daomao wrote on paper: "Calamity: on the third month, second day, comes the feast—the state and house are auspicious but the person is imperiled."
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi fell ill. Daomao wrote on a slip of paper, "Calamity arrives on the third month, second day, at the feast—the realm and house will prosper, but the man himself is in peril."

sentences.zh: 會中和日，泌雖篤，強入。

translations.literal: On the Zhonghe day, though Mi was gravely ill, he forced himself to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: On the Zhonghe day, though Mi was desperately ill, he forced himself to attend court.

sentences.zh: 德宗見泌不能步，詔歸第，卒。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong saw that Mi could not walk, ordered him home, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong saw that Mi could no longer walk, ordered him home, and he died.

sentences.zh: 是日北軍謀亂，仗士禽斬之。

translations.literal: That same day the Northern Army plotted rebellion; armed soldiers seized and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the Northern Army plotted rebellion; armed troops seized the conspirators and beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 李鵬為盛唐令，道茂曰：「君位止此，而冢息位宰相，次息亦大鎮，子孫百世。」

translations.literal: Li Peng was Magistrate of Shengtang. Daomao said: "Your rank stops here, but your eldest son will reach the chancellorship, the second son also a great frontier command, and posterity for a hundred generations."
translations.idiomatic: Li Peng was magistrate of Shengtang. Daomao said, "Your own rank will go no higher, but your eldest son will reach the chancellorship, your second will command a great frontier post, and your line will flourish for a hundred generations."

sentences.zh: 鵬卒，後石至宰相，福歷七鎮，諸孫通顯云。

translations.literal: Peng died; afterward Shi reached the chancellorship, Fu held seven frontier commands, and the grandsons all rose to prominence, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Peng died. Thereafter Shi rose to chancellor, Fu held seven frontier commands, and the grandsons all attained high office, so it is recorded.
